verses.1:1: And it came to pass, after Alexander the son of Philip, the Macedonian, who went forth from the land of Kittim, struck down Darius, king of the Persians and Medes, that he reigned in his stead, having first reigned over Greece.
verses.1:2: And he waged many wars, captured strongholds, and slew kings,
verses.1:3: and he passed through to the ends of the earth, and took the spoils of a multitude of nations. And the earth was quiet before him, and he was exalted, and his heart was lifted up.
verses.1:4: And he gathered an exceedingly mighty army, and ruled over countries, nations, and principalities, and they became tributary to him.
verses.1:5: And after these things he fell upon his bed, and knew that he was dying.
verses.1:6: Then he called his honored servants, who had been brought up with him from youth, and divided his kingdom among them while he was still alive.
verses.1:7: And Alexander reigned twelve years, and died.
verses.1:8: And his servants took dominion, each in his own place.
verses.1:9: And they all put diadems upon themselves after his death, and their sons after them for many years; and they multiplied evils in the earth.
verses.1:10: And there came forth from them a sinful root, Antiochus Epiphanes, son of Antiochus the king, who had been a hostage in Rome; and he began to reign in the one hundred and thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks.
verses.1:11: In those days there went forth from Israel a lawless son, and they persuaded many, saying, "Let us go and make a covenant with the Gentiles who are around us, for since we were separated from them, many evils have found us."
verses.1:12: And the word was pleasing in their eyes.
verses.1:13: And some of the people were eager, and went to the king; and they gave them authority to observe the ordinances of the Gentiles.
verses.1:14: And they built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the customs of the Gentiles.
verses.1:15: And they made themselves uncircumcised, and turned away from the holy covenant; and they yoked themselves to the Gentiles, and sold themselves to do evil.
verses.1:16: And the kingdom was established before Antiochus, and he purposed to reign over the land of Egypt, that he might reign over the two kingdoms.
verses.1:17: And he entered into Egypt with a mighty force, with chariots and elephants, and with horsemen, and with a great fleet.
verses.1:18: And he waged war against Ptolemy, king of Egypt; and Ptolemy turned back before him and fled, and many fell wounded.
verses.1:19: And they captured the fortified cities in the land of Egypt, and he took the spoils of the land of Egypt.
verses.1:20: And Antiochus returned after striking down Egypt, in the one hundred and forty-third year; and he went up against Israel and Jerusalem with a mighty force.
verses.1:21: And he entered into the sanctuary in arrogance, and took the golden altar, and the lampstand of light and all its utensils,
verses.1:22: and the table of the showbread, and the vessels for drink offerings, and the bowls, and the golden censers, and the veil, and the crowns, and the golden adornment on the front of the temple; and he stripped it all off.
verses.1:23: And he took the silver and the gold, and the precious vessels; and he took the hidden treasures which he found.
verses.1:24: And having taken all things, he departed to his own land. And they committed slaughter, and spoke with great arrogance.
verses.1:25: And there was great mourning upon Israel, in every place of theirs.
verses.1:26: And rulers and elders groaned; virgins and young men grew faint, and the beauty of the women faded.
verses.1:27: Every bridegroom took up a lamentation; she who sat in the bridal chamber was in mourning.
verses.1:28: And the land trembled for those who dwelt in it, and all the house of Jacob clothed itself with shame.
verses.1:29: After two full years, the king sent a chief collector of tribute to the cities of Judah, and he came to Jerusalem with a mighty force.
verses.1:30: And he spoke peaceful words to them in deceit, and they trusted him; then he fell upon the city suddenly, and struck it with a great blow, and destroyed many people from Israel.
verses.1:31: And he took the spoils of the city and burned it with fire, and tore down its houses and its walls all around,
verses.1:32: and he took the women and the children captive, and they took possession of the livestock.
verses.1:33: And they fortified the city of David with a great and strong wall, with strong towers, and it became a citadel for them.
verses.1:34: And they placed there a sinful nation, lawless men, and they strengthened themselves in it.
verses.1:35: And they stored up weapons and provisions, and having gathered the spoils of Jerusalem, they laid them up there; and it became a great snare,
verses.1:36: and it became an ambush against the sanctuary, and an evil adversary to Israel continually.
verses.1:37: And they shed innocent blood all around the sanctuary, and defiled the sanctuary.
verses.1:38: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled because of them, and she became a dwelling of strangers; she became a stranger to her own offspring, and her children forsook her.
verses.1:39: Her sanctuary was laid waste like a wilderness; her feasts were turned into mourning, her Sabbaths into reproach, her honor into contempt.
verses.1:40: According to her glory, her dishonor was multiplied, and her exaltation was turned into mourning.
verses.1:41: And the king wrote to his whole kingdom that all should be one people,
verses.1:42: and that each should forsake his own customs. And all the nations consented according to the word of the king.
verses.1:43: And many from Israel gladly accepted his worship, and sacrificed to idols, and profaned the Sabbath.
verses.1:44: And the king sent letters by the hand of messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, that they should follow customs foreign to the land,
verses.1:45: and forbid burnt offerings and sacrifices and drink offering from the sanctuary, and profane Sabbaths and feasts,
verses.1:46: and defile the sanctuary and the holy ones;
verses.1:47: to build pagan altars and shrines and idols, and to sacrifice swine and unclean animals,
verses.1:48: and to leave their sons uncircumcised, to make their souls abominable with every unclean thing and to profane them,
verses.1:49: so that they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.
verses.1:50: And whoever does not act according to the word of the king shall die.
verses.1:51: According to all these words he wrote to his kingdom, and he appointed overseers over all the people, and commanded the cities of Judah to offer sacrifice, city by city.
verses.1:52: And many of the people gathered together to them, everyone who forsook the law; and they did evil in the land,
verses.1:53: and drove Israel into secret places, into every place of refuge of theirs.
verses.1:54: And on the fifteenth day of Chislev, in the forty-fifth year, they built an abomination of desolation upon the altar; and in the cities of Judah all around they built pagan altars,
verses.1:55: and they burned incense at the windows of the houses and in the streets.
verses.1:56: And they tore in pieces the books of the law which they found, and burned them with fire.
verses.1:57: And wherever a book of the covenant was found with anyone, and if anyone adhered to the law, the decree of the king put him to death.
verses.1:58: In their might they did thus to Israel, to those who were found month by month in the cities.
verses.1:59: And on the twenty-fifth day of the month they offered sacrifice upon the pagan altar which was upon the altar.
verses.1:60: And according to the decree they put to death the women who had circumcised their children,
verses.1:61: and hanged the infants from their necks, and put to death their households and those who had circumcised them.
verses.1:62: And many in Israel were hanged. And they stood firm within themselves not to eat unclean things;
verses.1:63: and they chose to die, so that they might not be defiled by the foods and might not profane the holy covenant; and they died.
verses.1:64: And there was exceedingly great wrath upon Israel.
verses.2:1: In those days Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarim, arose from Jerusalem and dwelt in Modein.
verses.2:2: And he had five sons: John, who was surnamed Gaddis,
verses.2:5: Eleazar, who was called Avaran, and Jonathan, who was called Sapphus.
verses.2:6: And he saw the blasphemies that were being committed in Judah and in Jerusalem,
verses.2:7: and he said, "Woe is me! Why was I born for this, to see the calamities of my people and the ruin of the holy city, and to sit there when it was delivered into the hand of enemies, and the sanctuary into the hand of strangers?
verses.2:8: Her temple has become like a glorious man;
verses.2:9: the vessels of glory have been carried away captive; her infants have been slain in her streets, and her young men by the sword of the enemy.
verses.2:10: What nation has not inherited kingdoms and has not seized her spoils?
verses.2:11: All her adornment has been taken away; instead of a free woman, she has become a bondwoman.
verses.2:12: And behold, our sanctuary and our beauty and our glory have been laid waste, and the nations have profaned them.
verses.2:13: Why should we live any longer?"
verses.2:14: Then Mattathias and his sons tore their garments, put on sackcloth, and mourned exceedingly.
verses.2:15: Now the officers from the king who were enforcing the apostasy came to the city of Modein, so that they might offer sacrifice.
verses.2:16: And many from Israel came to them, and Mattathias and his sons gathered together.
verses.2:17: Then the officers from the king answered and spoke to Mattathias, saying, "You are a ruler, honorable and great in this city, and strengthened with sons and brethren.
verses.2:18: Now come forward first and carry out the decree of the king, as all the nations have done, and the rulers of Judah, and those who remain in Jerusalem; and you and your house shall be among the friends of the king, and you and your sons shall be honored with silver and gold and many gifts."
verses.2:19: And Mattathias answered and said with a loud voice, "Even if all the nations that are in the house of the king's dominion obey him, so that each one departs from the worship of his fathers, and they have chosen his commandments,
verses.2:20: yet I and my sons and my brethren will walk in the covenant of our fathers.
verses.2:21: Far be it from us to forsake the law and the ordinances.
verses.2:22: We will not obey the law of the king, to turn aside from our worship to the right hand or to the left."
verses.2:23: And when he had finished speaking these words, a Jewish man came forward in the sight of all to burn incense upon the altar in Modein, according to the decree of the king.
verses.2:24: And Mattathias saw it and was filled with zeal, and his inward parts trembled, and he stirred up his wrath according to the judgment; and he ran and slew him upon the altar.
verses.2:25: He also killed at that time the king's officer who was compelling them to sacrifice, and he tore down the altar.
verses.2:26: Thus he was zealous for the law, just as Phinehas did to Zimri the son of Salom.
verses.2:27: Then Mattathias cried out in the city with a loud voice, saying, "Everyone who is zealous for the law and maintains the covenant, let him come out after me!"
verses.2:28: So he and his sons fled into the mountains, and left behind all that they had in the city.
verses.2:29: Then many who were seeking righteousness and justice went down into the wilderness to dwell there,
verses.2:30: they and their sons, and their wives, and their livestock, because the evils had grown severe upon them.
verses.2:31: And it was reported to the king's men and to the forces that were in Jerusalem, the city of David, that men who had broken the commandment of the king had gone down into the hiding places in the wilderness.
verses.2:32: And many ran after them, and having overtaken them, they encamped against them and set battle in array against them on the Sabbath day.
verses.2:33: And they said to them, "Enough until now! Come out and do according to the word of the king, and you shall live."
verses.2:34: And they said, "We will not come out, nor will we do the word of the king, to profane the Sabbath day."
verses.2:35: Then they hastened to wage battle against them.
verses.2:36: And they did not answer them, nor did they hurl a stone at them, nor did they block up the hiding places,
verses.2:37: saying, "Let us all die in our innocence; heaven and earth bear witness for us that you destroy us without judgment."
verses.2:38: So they rose up against them in battle on the Sabbath; and they died, they and their wives and their children and their livestock, up to a thousand souls of men.
verses.2:39: And Mattathias and his friends learned of it, and they mourned over them exceedingly.
verses.2:40: And each man said to his neighbor, "If we all do as our brethren have done, and do not fight against the nations for our lives and our ordinances, they will now quickly destroy us from the earth."
verses.2:41: So they took counsel on that day, saying, "Every man who comes against us to battle on the Sabbath day, let us fight against him, and we shall by no means all die as our brethren died in the hiding places."
verses.2:42: Then there gathered to them a company of Hasideans, with mighty strength from Israel, everyone who offered himself willingly for the law.
verses.2:43: And all who were fleeing from the evils were added to them, and became a support to them.
verses.2:44: So they mustered a force, and struck down sinners in their anger and lawless men in their wrath; and the rest fled to the nations to be saved.
verses.2:45: And Mattathias and his sons went around and tore down their altars,
verses.2:46: and they circumcised all the uncircumcised boys whom he found within the borders of Israel, by force.
verses.2:47: They also pursued the sons of arrogance, and the work prospered in their hand.
verses.2:48: So they rescued the law out of the hand of the nations and out of the hand of the kings, and they did not give a horn to the sinner.
verses.2:49: Now the days of Mattathias drew near for him to die, and he said to his sons, "Now arrogance and rebuke have grown strong, and a time of overthrow and fierce wrath.
verses.2:50: And now, children, be zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers.
verses.2:51: Remember the deeds of our fathers which they did in their generations, and receive great glory and everlasting glory.
verses.2:52: Was not Abraham found faithful in testing, and righteousness was accounted to him?
verses.2:53: Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment, and became lord of Egypt.
verses.2:54: Phinehas our father, by showing great zeal, received the covenant of a holy priesthood.
verses.2:55: Joshua, by fulfilling the word, became a judge in Israel.
verses.2:56: Caleb, by bearing witness before the congregation, received a land as an inheritance.
verses.2:57: David, by his mercy, inherited the throne of an everlasting kingdom.
verses.2:58: Elijah, by showing great zeal for the law, was taken up as into heaven.
verses.2:59: Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, by believing, were saved out of the flame.
verses.2:60: Daniel, in his innocence, was delivered from the mouth of lions.
verses.2:61: And thus consider from generation to generation that all who hope in Him shall not grow weak.
verses.2:62: And do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory comes to dung and to worms.
verses.2:63: Today he shall be lifted up, and he shall by no means be found, because he has returned to his dust, and his thought has perished.
verses.2:64: And you, children, be strong and act courageously in your law, for in it you shall be glorified.
verses.2:65: And behold, Simeon your brother—I know that he is a man of counsel; listen to him all your days; he shall be a father to you.
verses.2:66: And Judas Maccabeus—he has been mighty in strength from his youth; he shall be to you a commander of the army, and you shall fight the battle of the peoples.
verses.2:67: And you shall gather to yourselves all the doers of the law, and execute vengeance for your people.
verses.2:68: Render recompense to the nations, and give heed to the commandments of the law."
verses.2:69: Then he blessed them, and was gathered to his fathers.
verses.2:70: And he died in the one hundred and forty-sixth year; and his sons buried him in the tombs of his fathers in Modein, and all Israel mourned for him with great lamentation.
verses.3:1: Then his son Judas, who was called Maccabeus, arose in his place.
verses.3:2: And all his brothers helped him, and all who had joined themselves to his father, and they fought the battle of Israel with gladness.
verses.3:3: And he extended glory for his people; he put on a breastplate like a giant and girded on his weapons of war; he waged battles, shielding the camp with the sword.
verses.3:4: And he was like a lion in his deeds, and like a young lion roaring for prey.
verses.3:5: And he pursued the lawless, searching them out, and those who troubled his people he consumed with flames.
verses.3:6: And the lawless shrank back in fear of him, and all the workers of lawlessness were thrown into confusion, and deliverance prospered in his hand.
verses.3:7: And he embittered many kings, and made Jacob glad by his deeds, and forever his memorial is for a blessing.
verses.3:8: And he passed through the cities of Judah, and utterly destroyed the ungodly from it, and turned away wrath from Israel.
verses.3:9: And he was renowned to the farthest end of the earth, and he gathered together those who were perishing.
verses.3:10: Then Apollonius gathered Gentiles, and from Samaria a great army, to wage war against Israel.
verses.3:11: And Judas learned of it, and went out to meet him, and struck him down and slew him; and many fell wounded, and the rest fled.
verses.3:12: And they took their spoils, and Judas took the sword of Apollonius, and he fought with it all his days.
verses.3:13: Now Seron, the commander of the army of Syria, heard that Judas had gathered a company and an assembly of faithful men with him, and of those going out to war.
verses.3:14: And he said, "I will make a name for myself, and I will be glorified in the kingdom, and I will wage war against Judas and those with him, and those who despise the word of the king."
verses.3:15: And he proceeded, and a strong host of the ungodly went up with him to help him, to execute vengeance upon the children of Israel.
verses.3:16: And he drew near as far as the ascent of Methoron; and Judas went out to meet him with very few men.
verses.3:17: And when they saw the host coming to meet him, they said to Judas, "How shall we, being so few, be able to fight against so great a multitude? And we are faint, having eaten nothing today."
verses.3:18: And Judas said, "It is easy for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and there is no difference in the sight of Heaven to save by many or by few.
verses.3:19: For victory in battle does not rest in the multitude of an army, but rather strength is from Heaven.
verses.3:20: They come against us in an abundance of insolence and lawlessness, to destroy us and our wives and our children, to plunder us.
verses.3:21: But we fight for our lives and our laws.
verses.3:22: And He Himself will crush them before our face; and as for you, do not be afraid of them."
verses.3:23: Now when he ceased speaking, he rushed upon them suddenly, and Seron and his host were crushed before him.
verses.3:24: And they pursued them down the descent of Beth-horon as far as the plain; and about eight hundred men from among them fell, and the rest fled into the land of the Philistines.
verses.3:25: And the fear of Judas and his brothers began, and terror fell upon the nations all around them.
verses.3:26: And his name reached as far as the king, and every nation recounted the battles of Judas.
verses.3:27: Now when King Antiochus heard these reports, he burned with wrath; and he sent and gathered all the forces of his kingdom, an exceedingly strong host.
verses.3:28: And he opened his treasury, and gave pay to his forces for the year; and he commanded them to be ready for a year for every need.
verses.3:29: And he saw that the silver had failed from the treasuries, and that the tributes of the country were small because of the dissension and calamity which he had brought about in the land, to abolish the laws which had been from the earliest days.
verses.3:30: And he feared lest he might not have enough, as once and twice before, for the expenses and the gifts which he had formerly given with a lavish hand,
verses.3:31: And he was exceedingly perplexed in his soul; and he resolved to go into Persia, and to collect the tributes of the countries, and to gather much silver.
verses.3:32: And he left Lysias, an honorable man and of royal lineage, over the affairs of the king, from the river Euphrates to the borders of Egypt,
verses.3:33: and to bring up his son Antiochus until he returned.
verses.3:34: And he delivered to him half of the forces and the elephants, and gave him orders concerning all that he desired, and concerning all the inhabitants of Judea and Jerusalem,
verses.3:35: to send an army against them, to cast out and destroy the strength of Israel and the remnant of Jerusalem, and to remove its memorial from the place,
verses.3:36: and to settle foreigners within all their borders, and to distribute their land by lot.
verses.3:37: So the king took the remaining half of the forces and departed from Antioch, the city of his kingdom, in the one hundred and forty-seventh year; and he crossed the Euphrates River and passed through the upper countries.
verses.3:38: Then Lysias chose Ptolemy the son of Dorymenes, Nicanor, and Gorgias, mighty men among the friends of the king.
verses.3:39: And he sent with them forty thousand men and seven thousand horsemen, to go into the land of Judah and destroy it according to the word of the king.
verses.3:40: So they set out with all their army and came, and encamped near Emmaus in the plain country.
verses.3:41: And the merchants of the country heard of their fame, and took very much silver and gold and servants, and came into the camp to take the children of Israel as servants; and forces of Syria and of the land of the Philistines joined them.
verses.3:42: Now Judas and his brothers saw that evils had multiplied, and that the armies would encamp within their borders; and they learned of the words of the kingdom which he had commanded to do to the people for destruction and utter ruin.
verses.3:43: And each one said to his neighbor, "Let us raise up the ruin of our people and of the sanctuary."
verses.3:44: And the congregation gathered together to be ready for battle, and to pray and ask for mercy and compassion.
verses.3:45: Now Jerusalem lay uninhabited like a wilderness; there was none of her offspring going in or going out; and the sanctuary was trampled down, and sons of foreigners were in the citadel, a lodging place among the Gentiles; and joy was taken away from Jacob, and the flute and the harp ceased.
verses.3:46: So they gathered together and came to Mizpah, opposite Jerusalem, because Mizpah had formerly been a place of prayer for Israel.
verses.3:47: And they fasted on that day, and put on sackcloth and put ashes upon their heads, and tore their garments.
verses.3:48: And they unrolled the book of the law, concerning those things about which the Gentiles inquired of the likenesses of their idols.
verses.3:49: And they brought the garments of the priesthood, and the firstfruits, and the tithes; and they raised up the Nazirites who had completed their days;
verses.3:50: and they cried aloud toward Heaven, saying, "What shall we do with these, and where shall we take them?
verses.3:51: And Your sanctuary has been trampled down and profaned, and Your priests are in mourning and humiliation.
verses.3:52: And behold, the Gentiles are gathered together against us to destroy us; You know what they devise against us.
verses.3:53: How shall we be able to stand before their face, unless You help us?"
verses.3:54: Then they sounded the trumpets and cried out with a loud voice.
verses.3:55: And after this Judas appointed leaders of the people: commanders of thousands, and commanders of hundreds, and commanders of fifties, and commanders of tens.
verses.3:56: And he told those who were building a house, and those who were betrothed to wives, and those who were planting vineyards, and those who were fearful, that each one should return to his own house according to the law.
verses.3:57: Then the host moved out, and they encamped to the south of Emmaus.
verses.3:58: And Judas said, "Gird yourselves, and be valiant men; and be ready in the morning to fight against these Gentiles who are assembled against us to destroy us and our sanctuary.
verses.3:59: For it is better for us to die in battle than to look upon the calamities of our nation and of the sanctuary.
verses.3:60: Yet as the will in Heaven may be, so He will do."
verses.4:1: Now Gorgias took five thousand men and a thousand chosen horsemen, and the army departed by night,
verses.4:2: so as to fall upon the camp of the Jews and strike them suddenly; and the men of the citadel were his guides.
verses.4:3: And Judas heard of it, and he himself and the mighty men departed to strike the army of the king that was in Emmaus,
verses.4:4: while the forces were still scattered away from the camp.
verses.4:5: And Gorgias came to the camp of Judas by night, and found no one; so he searched for them in the mountains, for he said, "These men are fleeing from us."
verses.4:6: And at daybreak Judas appeared in the plain with three thousand men; yet they did not have shields and swords such as they desired.
verses.4:7: And they saw a strong camp of the Gentiles clad in armor, with cavalry encircling it; and these were men trained in war.
verses.4:8: And Judas said to the men who were with him, "Do not fear their multitude, and do not be dismayed at their onslaught.
verses.4:9: Remember how our fathers were saved at the Red Sea, when Pharaoh pursued them with an army.
verses.4:10: And now let us cry out to Heaven, whether He will favor us, and remember the covenant of the fathers, and crush this army before our face today.
verses.4:11: Then all the nations shall know that there is One who redeems and saves Israel."
verses.4:12: And the foreigners lifted up their eyes and saw them positioned close opposite them,
verses.4:13: and they went out from the camp to battle, and those who were with Judas sounded the trumpets.
verses.4:14: And they joined battle, and the Gentiles were crushed and fled into the plain.
verses.4:15: And all those in the rear fell by the sword; and they pursued them as far as Gazara, and to the plains of Judea, and of Azotus and Jamnia, and about three thousand of their men fell.
verses.4:16: Then Judas and the army returned from pursuing after them,
verses.4:17: and he said to the people, "Do not covet the spoils, for a battle is before us,
verses.4:18: and Gorgias and the army are in the mountain near us; rather, stand now against our enemies and fight them, and after these things take spoils, and with confidence."
verses.4:19: While Judas was still finishing these words, a certain detachment appeared peering out from the mountain.
verses.4:20: And they saw that the army had been put to flight and that the camp was being set on fire; for the smoke that was seen revealed what had happened.
verses.4:21: Now when they perceived these things, they were exceedingly afraid; and seeing also the army of Judas in the plain ready for battle,
verses.4:22: they all fled into the land of the Philistines.
verses.4:23: Then Judas turned back to plunder the camp, and he took much gold and silver, and blue, and purple, and sea-purple, and great riches.
verses.4:24: And as they returned, they sang hymns and blessed Heaven: "For His mercy is good forever."
verses.4:25: And a great deliverance came to Israel in that day.
verses.4:26: Now as many of the foreigners as escaped came and reported to Lysias all the things that had happened.
verses.4:27: And when he heard it all, he was confounded and disheartened, because things had not happened to Israel such as he desired, nor had events turned out as the king had commanded him.
verses.4:28: And in the following year he mustered sixty thousand chosen men and five thousand horsemen, so as to subdue them in war.
verses.4:29: And they came into Idumea and encamped at Bethzur, and Judas met them with ten thousand men.
verses.4:30: And he saw the mighty army, and he prayed and said, "Blessed are You, O Savior of Israel, who crushed the onslaught of the mighty one by the hand of Your servant David, and delivered the camp of the Philistines into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul and his armorbearer.
verses.4:31: Shut up this army into the hands of Your people Israel, and let them be put to shame in their army and their horsemen.
verses.4:32: Give them cowardice, and melt the boldness of their strength, and let them be shaken at their destruction.
verses.4:33: Cast them down by the sword of those who love You, and let all who have seen Your name praise You with hymns."
verses.4:34: And they clashed with one another, and about five thousand men fell from the army of Lysias; indeed, they fell right before them.
verses.4:35: Now when Lysias saw the rout that had come upon his own ranks, and the boldness that had come upon those of Judas, and how ready they were either to live or to die nobly, he departed to Antioch; and he recruited mercenaries, intending, once he had grown greater in number, to come again into Judea.
verses.4:36: Then Judas and his brothers said, "Behold, our enemies are crushed; let us go up to cleanse the sanctuary and dedicate it."
verses.4:37: So all the army was gathered together, and they went up to Mount Zion.
verses.4:38: And they saw our sanctuary laid desolate, and the altar profaned, and the gates burned down, and shrubs growing in the courts as in a forest or as on one of the mountains, and the priests' chambers torn down.
verses.4:39: And they tore their garments, and made a great lamentation, and put ashes upon their heads.
verses.4:40: And they fell on their faces to the ground, and sounded the signal trumpets, and cried out to Heaven.
verses.4:41: Then Judas appointed men to fight against those who were in the citadel, until he should cleanse the sanctuary.
verses.4:42: And he chose blameless priests who delighted in the law;
verses.4:43: and they cleansed the sanctuary, and carried away the stones of defilement to an unclean place.
verses.4:44: And they took counsel concerning the altar of burnt offering that had been profaned, as to what they should do with it.
verses.4:45: And a good counsel came to them, to tear it down, lest it should ever become a reproach to them because the Gentiles had defiled it; so they tore down the altar.
verses.4:46: And they stored away the stones on the mountain of the house in a fitting place, until a prophet should come to give an answer concerning them.
verses.4:47: And they took whole stones according to the law, and built a new altar like the former one.
verses.4:48: And they built the sanctuary and the inner parts of the house, and he consecrated the courts.
verses.4:49: And they made new holy vessels, and brought the lampstand, and the altar of burnt offerings and of incense, and the table into the temple.
verses.4:50: And they burned incense upon the altar, and lit the lamps that were upon the lampstand, and they gave light in the temple.
verses.4:51: And they set loaves upon the table, and spread out the curtains; and they finished all the works that they had done.
verses.4:52: And they rose early in the morning on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month, which is the month of Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-eighth year.
verses.4:53: And they offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings which they had made.
verses.4:54: At the very season and on the very day on which the Gentiles had profaned it, on that day it was dedicated with songs, and harps, and lutes, and cymbals.
verses.4:55: And all the people fell upon their faces, and worshiped, and blessed toward Heaven the One who had prospered them.
verses.4:56: And they celebrated the dedication of the altar for eight days, and offered burnt offerings with gladness, and sacrificed a sacrifice of deliverance and praise.
verses.4:57: And they adorned the front of the temple with golden crowns and small shields, and he dedicated the gates and the priests' chambers, and they fitted them with doors.
verses.4:58: And there was exceedingly great gladness among the people, and the reproach of the Gentiles was turned away.
verses.4:59: And Judas and his brothers and all the assembly of Israel ordained that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their seasons, year by year, for eight days, from the twenty-fifth day of the month of Chislev, with gladness and joy.
verses.4:60: And at that time they built up Mount Zion with high walls and strong towers all around, lest the Gentiles should ever come and trample them down, as they had done before.
verses.4:61: And they stationed a force there to guard it, and they fortified it to guard Bethzur, so that the people might have a stronghold facing Idumea.
verses.5:1: Now it came to pass, when the nations round about heard that the altar had been built and the sanctuary dedicated as before, that they were exceedingly angry.
verses.5:2: And they took counsel to destroy the race of Jacob who were in their midst, and they began to slay among the people and to cut them off.
verses.5:3: Then Judas waged war against the sons of Esau in Judea at Acrabattene, because they were besieging Israel; and he struck them with a great blow, and humbled them, and took their spoil.
verses.5:4: He also remembered the wickedness of the sons of Baean, who were a snare and a stumbling block to the people by lying in wait for them along the roads.
verses.5:5: And they were shut up by him in the towers, and he encamped against them, and devoted them to destruction, and burned its towers with fire, together with all who were in them.
verses.5:6: Then he crossed over against the sons of Ammon, and found a mighty force and a great host, with Timothy as their commander.
verses.5:7: And he engaged in many battles against them, and they were crushed before his face, and he struck them down.
verses.5:8: He also seized Jaze and its daughter towns, and returned to Judea.
verses.5:9: Now the nations in Gilead gathered together against Israel, against those who were within their borders, to destroy them; and they fled to Dathema, the stronghold.
verses.5:10: And they sent letters to Judas and his brethren, saying, "The nations round about us have gathered together against us to destroy us,
verses.5:11: and they are preparing to come and capture the stronghold to which we have fled; and Timothy is the commander of their army.
verses.5:12: Now therefore, come and deliver us from their hand, for a multitude of us have fallen.
verses.5:13: And all our brethren who were in the territory of Tubias have been put to death, and they have carried captive their wives and their children and their possessions, and have destroyed there about one thousand men."
verses.5:14: While the letters were still being read, behold, other messengers arrived from Galilee with their garments torn, reporting according to these words,
verses.5:15: saying, "Those from Ptolemais and Tyre and Sidon, and all Galilee of the foreigners, have gathered together against them to consume us."
verses.5:16: Now when Judas and the people heard these words, a great assembly gathered together to take counsel on what they should do for their brethren who were in distress and under attack by him.
verses.5:17: And Judas said to Simon his brother, "Choose men for yourself, and go and deliver your brethren in Galilee; and I and Jonathan my brother will go into Gilead."
verses.5:18: And he left Joseph the son of Zechariah, and Azariah, a leader of the people, with the rest of the army in Judea to guard it;
verses.5:19: and he commanded them, saying, "Take charge of this people, and do not engage in battle against the nations until we return."
verses.5:20: And three thousand men were allotted to Simon to go into Galilee, and eight thousand men to Judas for Gilead.
verses.5:21: So Simon went into Galilee and engaged in many battles against the nations; and the nations were crushed before his face.
verses.5:22: And he pursued them as far as the cities of Ptolemais; and about three thousand men of the nations fell, and he took their spoil.
verses.5:23: And he took them from Galilee and from Arbacta, together with their wives and children, and all that belonged to them, and they brought them into Judea with great gladness.
verses.5:24: Now Judas Maccabeus and Jonathan his brother crossed the Jordan and marched a three days' journey in the wilderness.
verses.5:25: And they met the Nabateans, who received them peaceably and recounted to them all that had happened to their brethren in Gilead:
verses.5:26: that many of them are shut up in Bossora and Bossor, in Alama, Casphor, Makeb, and Carnein—all these cities are fortified and great—
verses.5:27: and in the remaining cities of Gilead they are shut up; and for tomorrow they are set to encamp against the strongholds, and to capture and destroy all of them in one day.
verses.5:28: Then Judas and his army suddenly turned back by way of the wilderness to Bosor; and he captured the city, and slew every male with the edge of the sword, and took all their spoil, and burned it with fire.
verses.5:29: And he departed from there by night and marched as far as the stronghold.
verses.5:30: And when morning came, they lifted up their eyes, and behold, a great multitude without number, carrying ladders and siege engines to capture the stronghold; and they were fighting against them.
verses.5:31: And Judas saw that the battle had begun, and that the cry of the city went up to heaven, with trumpets and a loud shout;
verses.5:32: and he said to the men of the army, "Fight today for our brethren."
verses.5:33: Then he went out in three companies behind them; and he sounded the trumpets, and they cried out in prayer.
verses.5:34: And the army of Timothy recognized that it was Maccabeus, and they fled before his face, and he struck them with a great slaughter; and about eight thousand of their men fell on that day.
verses.5:35: Then he turned aside to Maapha and fought against it, and captured it, and slew every male in it, and took its spoil, and burned it with fire.
verses.5:36: From there he departed and seized Chasphoth, Maked, Bosor, and the remaining cities of Gilead.
verses.5:37: Now after these things Timothy gathered another army, and encamped opposite Raphon across the brook.
verses.5:38: And Judas sent men to spy out the camp; and they reported to him, saying, "All the nations round about you have gathered together to them, an exceedingly great force.
verses.5:39: And Arabs have been hired to help them, and they are encamped across the brook, ready to come against you in battle." And Judas went out to meet them.
verses.5:40: And Timothy said to the commanders of his army, as Judas and his army drew near to the brook of water, "If he crosses over to us first, we will not be able to withstand him, for he will surely prevail against us.
verses.5:41: But if he is afraid and encamps on the other side of the river, we will cross over to him."
verses.5:42: Now when Judas drew near to the brook of water, he stationed the scribes of the people by the brook and commanded them, saying, "Do not permit any man to encamp, but let all come into the battle."
verses.5:43: And he crossed over against them first, and all his people before him; and all the nations were crushed before his face, and they threw away all their weapons and fled to the sacred precinct in Carnain.
verses.5:44: And they seized the city, and burned the sacred precinct with fire, together with all who were in it; so Carnain was overthrown and could no longer stand before Judas.
verses.5:45: Then Judas gathered all Israel who were in Gilead, from the least to the greatest, together with their wives and their children and their possessions, an exceedingly great company, to come into the land of Judah.
verses.5:46: And they came as far as Ephron; now this was a great city at the entrance, exceedingly strong; it was not possible to turn aside from it to the right or to the left, but only to pass through the midst of it.
verses.5:47: And the people of the city shut them out, and blocked up the gates with stones.
verses.5:48: Then Judas sent to them with words of peace, saying, "I will pass through your land to go into our own land; and no one will harm you; we will only march through on foot." Yet they would not open to him.
verses.5:49: So Judas gave orders to proclaim in the camp that each man should encamp in the place where he was.
verses.5:50: And the men of the city encamped, and they fought against the city all that day and all that night, and the city was delivered into his hands.
verses.5:51: And he destroyed every male with the edge of the sword, and uprooted it, and took the spoil of the city, and marched through the city over the slain.
verses.5:52: Then they crossed the Jordan into the great plain opposite Bethshan.
verses.5:53: And Judas kept gathering together those who lagged behind and encouraging the people all along the way, until he came into the land of Judah.
verses.5:54: And they went up to Mount Zion with gladness and joy, and offered burnt offerings, because not one of them had fallen until they returned in peace.
verses.5:55: Now in the days when Judas and Jonathan were in Gilead, and Simon his brother was in Galilee opposite Ptolemais,
verses.5:56: Joseph the son of Zechariah, and Zechariah, the commanders of the forces, heard of the valiant deeds and the warfare that they had accomplished;
verses.5:57: and they said, "Let us also make a name for ourselves, and let us go to fight against the nations round about us."
verses.5:58: So they gave orders to the men of the force who were with them, and marched against Jamnia.
verses.5:59: And Gorgias and his men came out of the city to meet them in battle.
verses.5:60: And Joseph and Azariah were routed and pursued as far as the borders of Judea; and about two thousand men of the people of Israel fell on that day.
verses.5:61: Thus a great rout occurred among the people, because they did not listen to Judas and his brethren, supposing that he would do valiant deeds.
verses.5:62: But they were not of the seed of those men through whose hand the deliverance of Israel was given.
verses.5:63: And the man Judas and his brethren were greatly glorified before all Israel and all the nations, wherever their name was heard;
verses.5:64: and people gathered together to them, praising them.
verses.5:65: Then Judas and his brethren went forth and fought against the sons of Esau in the land toward the south, and he struck Hebron and its daughter towns; and he tore down its stronghold and burned its towers round about.
verses.5:66: And he departed to go into the land of the foreigners, and passed through Samaria.
verses.5:67: On that day priests fell in battle while he desired to act valiantly, when he went out to battle recklessly.
verses.5:68: Then Judas turned aside to Azotus, the land of the foreigners, and tore down their altars, and burned the carved images of their gods, and plundered the spoil of the cities, and returned to Judea.
verses.6:1: Now King Antiochus was passing through the upper provinces, and he heard that in Elymais in Persia there was a city renowned for wealth, silver, and gold;
verses.6:2: and that the temple in it was exceedingly rich, and there were golden shields, breastplates, and weapons, which Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian king who first reigned over the Greeks, had left there.
verses.6:3: So he came and sought to capture the city and plunder it, but he was not able, because the matter became known to the people of the city.
verses.6:4: And they rose up against him for battle, so he fled and departed from there with great grief to return to Babylon.
verses.6:5: And someone came to him in Persia reporting that the armies that had gone into the land of Judah had been routed;
verses.6:6: that Lysias had marched first with a strong force and had been driven back before them, and that they had grown strong through the weapons they had taken from the armies they had cut down;
verses.6:7: and that they had torn down the abomination he had built upon the altar in Jerusalem, and had surrounded the sanctuary with high walls as before, and also Beth-zur, his city.
verses.6:8: Now it came to pass, when the king heard these words, that he was astounded and exceedingly shaken; and he fell upon his bed and sank into sickness from grief, because things had not turned out for him as he had intended.
verses.6:9: And he remained there many days, because great grief was renewed upon him, and he reckoned that he was dying.
verses.6:10: So he summoned all his friends and said to them, "Sleep departs from my eyes, and my heart has sunk from anxiety.
verses.6:11: And I said in my heart, 'To what tribulation have I come, and to what a great flood, in which I now am? For I was kind and beloved in my authority.'
verses.6:12: But now I remember the evils that I did in Jerusalem; and I took all the silver and gold vessels that were in it, and I sent forth to destroy the inhabitants of Judah without cause.
verses.6:13: I know that on account of these things these evils have found me; and behold, I am perishing in great grief in a foreign land."
verses.6:14: Then he summoned Philip, one of his friends, and appointed him over all his kingdom.
verses.6:15: And he gave him the diadem, his robe, and the signet ring, to guide Antiochus his son and raise him up to reign.
verses.6:16: And King Antiochus died there in the one hundred and forty-ninth year.
verses.6:17: And Lysias learned that the king had died, and he appointed Antiochus his son, whom he had raised from his youth, to reign in his place; and he called his name Eupator.
verses.6:18: Now those from the citadel were hemming Israel in around the sanctuary, continually seeking evil and providing support for the Gentiles.
verses.6:19: So Judas resolved to destroy them, and he assembled all the people to lay siege against them
verses.6:20: in the one hundred and fiftieth year; and he built catapult platforms and siege engines against them.
verses.6:21: And some went out from it, from the blockade, and some of the ungodly from Israel joined themselves to them.
verses.6:22: And they went to the king and said, "How long will you not execute judgment and avenge our brethren?
verses.6:23: We were well pleased to serve your father, to walk by the words he spoke, and to follow his decrees;
verses.6:24: for on account of this those of our own people became estranged from us; moreover, as many of us as were found were put to death, and our inheritances were plundered.
verses.6:25: And they did not stretch out their hand against us only, but also against all their borders.
verses.6:26: And behold, today they have encamped against the citadel in Jerusalem to capture it; and they have fortified the sanctuary and Beth-zur.
verses.6:27: And if you do not forestall them swiftly, they will do greater things than these, and you will not be able to restrain them."
verses.6:28: And the king was angry when he heard this; and he gathered all his friends, the commanders of his army, and those in charge of the cavalry;
verses.6:29: and from other kings and from the islands of the seas, mercenary forces came to him.
verses.6:30: And the number of his forces was one hundred thousand foot soldiers, and twenty thousand horsemen, and thirty-two elephants trained for war.
verses.6:31: And they came through Idumea and encamped against Beth-zur, and fought for many days and built siege engines; but those within came out and burned them with fire, and fought valiantly.
verses.6:32: Then Judas departed from the citadel and encamped at Beth-zechariah, opposite the camp of the king.
verses.6:33: And the king rose early in the morning and led the army forth in fierce eagerness along the road to Beth-zechariah; and the forces arrayed themselves for battle, and they sounded the trumpets.
verses.6:34: And to the elephants they showed the blood of grapes and mulberries, to arouse them for battle.
verses.6:35: And they distributed the beasts among the phalanxes, and stationed beside each elephant one thousand men armored in chain mail, with bronze helmets upon their heads; and five hundred chosen horsemen were assigned to each beast.
verses.6:36: These were stationed beforehand wherever the beast was; and wherever it went, they went along with it, and did not depart from it.
verses.6:37: And upon them were strong, covered wooden towers, on every beast, fastened upon them with harnesses; and on each were thirty-two men fighting upon them, along with its Indian driver.
verses.6:38: And the rest of the cavalry he stationed on this side and on that, on the two flanks of the army, harassing the enemy while protected among the phalanxes.
verses.6:39: Now when the sun shone upon the golden shields, the mountains glistened from them and blazed like torches of fire.
verses.6:40: And part of the king's army was spread out upon the high mountains, and some upon the low ground; and they advanced steadily and in order.
verses.6:41: And all who heard the sound of their multitude, the marching of the multitude, and the clashing of weapons were shaken; for the army was exceedingly great and mighty.
verses.6:42: Then Judas and his army drew near for battle, and six hundred men of the king's army fell.
verses.6:43: And Eleazar, called Savaran, saw one of the beasts armored with royal breastplates, and it was taller than all the other beasts, and it appeared that the king was upon it.
verses.6:44: So he gave himself to save his people and to win for himself an everlasting name.
verses.6:45: And he ran boldly toward it into the midst of the phalanx, slaying to the right and to the left, so that they split apart from before him on this side and on that.
verses.6:46: And he crept beneath the elephant, and thrust from beneath it and slew it; and it fell to the ground upon him, and he died there.
verses.6:47: And they saw the strength of the kingdom and the fierce onset of the forces, and they turned away from them.
verses.6:48: Now troops from the king's army went up to meet them toward Jerusalem, and the king encamped in Judea and against Mount Zion.
verses.6:49: And he made peace with those of Beth-zur, and they went out of the city, because they had no food there to endure a siege in it, since it was a sabbath for the land.
verses.6:50: So the king took possession of Beth-zur and stationed a garrison there to guard it.
verses.6:51: And he encamped against the sanctuary for many days, and set up there catapult platforms, siege engines, fire-throwers, stone-throwers, scorpions for shooting arrows, and slings.
verses.6:52: And they also built siege engines to match their siege engines, and fought for many days.
verses.6:53: But there was no food in the sanctuary, because it was the seventh year, and those who had been brought safely into Judea from among the Gentiles had consumed the remainder of the provisions;
verses.6:54: and only a few men were left in the sanctuary, because the famine prevailed over them; and they were scattered, each man to his own place.
verses.6:55: Now Lysias heard that Philip, whom King Antiochus while still alive had appointed to raise his son Antiochus to reign,
verses.6:56: had returned from Persia and Media, along with the king's forces that had marched with him, and that he was seeking to take control of the affairs of state.
verses.6:57: So they made haste and urged one another to depart; and he said to the king, the commanders of the army, and the men, "We are growing weaker day by day, our food is scarce, the place we are besieging is strong, and the affairs of the kingdom press upon us.
verses.6:58: Now therefore let us give the right hand to these men, and make peace with them and with all their nation,
verses.6:59: and confirm to them that they may walk in their laws as before; for on account of their laws, which we abolished, they became angry and did all these things."
verses.6:60: And the word was pleasing in the sight of the king and the rulers, so he sent to them to make peace, and they accepted it.
verses.6:61: And the king and the rulers swore an oath to them upon these terms, and they came out of the stronghold.
verses.6:62: Then the king entered Mount Zion and saw the fortification of the place; and he broke the oath that he had sworn, and gave command and tore down the wall all around.
verses.6:63: And they departed in haste, and he returned to Antioch, and found Philip in control of the city; and he fought against him and took the city by force.
verses.7:1: In the fifty-first year Demetrius the son of Seleucus went out from Rome, and went up with a few men to a city by the sea, and reigned there.
verses.7:2: And it came to pass, as he was entering into the house of the kingdom of his fathers, that the forces seized Antiochus and Lysias to bring them to him.
verses.7:3: And the matter became known to him, and he said, "Do not show me their faces."
verses.7:4: And the forces slew them, and Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom.
verses.7:5: And all the lawless and ungodly men from Israel came to him, and Alcimus was leading them, desiring to serve as priest.
verses.7:6: And they accused the people before the king, saying, "Judas and his brethren have destroyed all your friends, and he has scattered us from our land.
verses.7:7: Now therefore send a man whom you trust, and let him go and see all the utter destruction which he has done to us and to the country of the king, and he has punished them and all who help them."
verses.7:8: Then the king chose Bacchides, one of the king's friends, who ruled in the region beyond the river, and was great in the kingdom and faithful to the king.
verses.7:9: And he sent him and the ungodly Alcimus, and they established the priesthood for him; and he commanded him to execute vengeance upon the children of Israel.
verses.7:10: So he departed and came with a great force into the land of Judah; and he sent messengers to Judas and to his brethren with peaceful words in deceit.
verses.7:11: And they did not give heed to their words, for they saw that they had come with a great force.
verses.7:12: And an assembly of scribes gathered together to Alcimus and Bacchides to seek what was just.
verses.7:13: And the Hasideans were the first among the children of Israel, and they sought peace from them;
verses.7:14: for they said, "A man who is a priest of the seed of Aaron has come with the forces, and he will not wrong us."
verses.7:15: And he spoke peaceful words with them, and swore to them, saying, "We will not seek evil against you nor against your friends."
verses.7:16: And they trusted him; and he seized sixty men of them, and slew them in one day, according to the words which he wrote:
verses.7:17: "The flesh of Your saints and their blood they poured out round about Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them."
verses.7:18: Then the fear and trembling of them fell upon all the people, for they said, "There is no truth and justice in them; for they have transgressed the agreement and the oath which they swore."
verses.7:19: And Bacchides departed from Jerusalem and encamped in Bezeth; and he sent and seized many of the men who had deserted to him, and some of the people, and slaughtered them into the great pit.
verses.7:20: And he committed the country to Alcimus and left a force with him to help him; and Bacchides departed to the king.
verses.7:21: And Alcimus strove for the high priesthood.
verses.7:22: And all who troubled their people gathered to him, and they gained mastery over the land of Judah, and inflicted a great blow in Israel.
verses.7:23: And Judas saw all the wickedness which Alcimus and those with him had done among the children of Israel, more than the Gentiles;
verses.7:24: and he went out into all the borders of Judea and round about, and executed vengeance upon the men and upon those who had deserted, and they were restrained from going into the country.
verses.7:25: Now when Alcimus saw that Judas and those with him had grown strong, and knew that he was able to withstand them, he returned to the king and accused them of wicked things.
verses.7:26: Then the king sent Nicanor, one of his honored princes, who hated and was hostile to Israel, and commanded him to destroy the people.
verses.7:27: And Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a great force, and sent to Judas and his brethren deceitfully with peaceful words, saying,
verses.7:28: "Let there be no battle between me and you; I will come with a few men, that I may see your faces in peace."
verses.7:29: And he came to Judas, and they greeted one another peacefully; yet the enemies were ready to snatch Judas away.
verses.7:30: And the matter became known to Judas, that he had come against him with deceit; and he was alarmed by him, and did not wish to see his face anymore.
verses.7:31: And Nicanor knew that his counsel had been uncovered, and he went out to meet Judas near Charpharsarama.
verses.7:32: And there fell of those with Nicanor about five thousand men, and they fled into the City of David.
verses.7:33: And after these things Nicanor went up to Mount Zion; and some of the priests came out from the sanctuary, and some of the elders of the people, to greet him peacefully and to show him the burnt offering that was being offered on behalf of the king.
verses.7:34: But he mocked them, and laughed them to scorn, and defiled them, and spoke arrogantly.
verses.7:35: And he swore in wrath, saying, "Unless Judas and his army are delivered into my hands now, then it shall be, if I return in peace, that I will burn up this house." And he went out in wrath.
verses.7:36: And the priests went in and stood before the altar and the temple, and wept and said,
verses.7:37: "You chose this house to have Your name called upon it, to be a house of prayer and supplication for Your people.
verses.7:38: Execute vengeance upon this man and upon his army, and let them fall by the sword; remember their blasphemies, and do not grant them continuance."
verses.7:39: Then Nicanor went out from Jerusalem, and they encamped in Beth-horon, and a force of Syria met him.
verses.7:40: And Judas encamped in Adasa with three thousand men; and Judas prayed and said,
verses.7:41: "When those from the king blasphemed, Your angel went out and struck down among them one hundred and eighty-five thousand.
verses.7:42: So crush this army before us today, and let the rest know that he has spoken wickedly against Your sanctuary; and judge him according to his wickedness."
verses.7:43: And the armies joined in battle on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and the army of Nicanor was crushed, and he himself fell first in the battle.
verses.7:44: Now when his army saw that Nicanor had fallen, they threw down their weapons and fled.
verses.7:45: And they pursued them a day's journey from Adasa until they came to Gazara, and they blew the signal trumpets behind them.
verses.7:46: And they came out from all the villages of Judea round about and outflanked them; and these turned back upon those, and they all fell by the sword, and not even one of them was left.
verses.7:47: And they took the spoils and the plunder, and they cut off the head of Nicanor and his right hand, which he had stretched out arrogantly, and brought them and stretched them out near Jerusalem.
verses.7:48: And the people rejoiced exceedingly, and they kept that day as a great day of gladness.
verses.7:49: And they decreed to keep this day year by year on the thirteenth day of Adar.
verses.7:50: And the land of Judah had rest for a few days.
verses.8:1: Now Judas heard of the fame of the Romans, that they were mighty in strength, and that they looked with favor upon all who joined themselves to them; and that with as many as joined themselves to them, and with as many as approached them, they established friendship,
verses.8:2: and that they were mighty in strength. They also recounted to him their wars and the valiant deeds which they carried out among the Galatians, and how they subdued them and brought them under tribute;
verses.8:3: and all that they did in the land of Spain to gain possession of the mines of silver and gold that were there;
verses.8:4: and they gained mastery over the whole place by their counsel and patience—even though the place was exceedingly far removed from them—and over the kings who came against them from the end of the earth, until they crushed them and struck them with a great blow, and the rest pay them tribute year by year.
verses.8:5: Moreover, Philip, and Perseus king of the Kittim, and those who rose up against them—they crushed them in war and subdued them.
verses.8:6: And Antiochus the Great, king of Asia, who marched against them to war having one hundred and twenty elephants, and cavalry, and chariots, and an exceedingly great force—he too was crushed by them.
verses.8:7: And they took him alive, and decreed that both he and those who reigned after him should pay them a great tribute, and give hostages and a stipulated partition,
verses.8:8: as well as the country of India, and Media, and Lydia, and some of their finest lands; and having taken them from him, they gave them to King Eumenes;
verses.8:9: and how those from Greece took counsel to come and destroy them,
verses.8:10: and the matter became known to them, and they sent against them a single general and fought against them; and many of them fell wounded, and they took their wives and their children captive, and plundered them, and took possession of their land, and tore down their strongholds, and plundered them, and brought them into bondage to this day.
verses.8:11: And the remaining kingdoms and the islands, as many as ever rose up against them, they destroyed and brought into subjection to themselves; but with their friends and those who relied upon them, they preserved friendship with them.
verses.8:12: And they subdued the kingdoms both near and far, and all who heard of their fame were afraid of them.
verses.8:13: Those whom they wish to help and to make kings, such ones reign; and those whom they wish, they depose; and they were exceedingly exalted.
verses.8:14: Yet in all these things, not one of them put on a diadem, nor did they clothe themselves in purple to be magnified by it.
verses.8:15: And they established a senate for themselves, and day by day three hundred and twenty men took counsel, deliberating continually concerning the people, that they might order themselves well.
verses.8:16: And they trust one man to rule over them year by year and to have dominion over all their land, and all obey that one man; and there is neither envy nor jealousy among them.
verses.8:17: Then Judas chose Eupolemus the son of John, the son of Accos, and Jason the son of Eleazar, and sent them to Rome to establish friendship and alliance with them,
verses.8:18: and to take away the yoke from them, for they saw that the kingdom of the Greeks was enslaving Israel into bondage.
verses.8:19: So they journeyed to Rome, and the way was exceedingly long; and they entered the senate house and spoke:
verses.8:20: "Judas, who is also called Maccabeus, and his brothers, and the people of the Jews have sent us to you to establish an alliance and peace with you, and that we may be enrolled as your allies and friends."
verses.8:21: And the proposal was pleasing in their sight.
verses.8:22: And this is the copy of the writing which they transcribed upon bronze tablets and sent to Jerusalem, to remain with them there as a memorial of peace and alliance:
verses.8:23: "May it be well with the Romans and with the nation of the Jews at sea and on land forever, and may sword and enemy be far removed from them.
verses.8:24: But if war should arise against Rome first, or against any of their allies in all their dominion,
verses.8:25: the nation of the Jews shall fight as their allies, as the occasion may prescribe for them, with a whole heart.
verses.8:26: And to those who wage war they shall neither give nor supply grain, weapons, silver, or ships, as it has seemed good to Rome; and they shall keep their obligations without receiving anything.
verses.8:27: Likewise, if war should befall the nation of the Jews first, the Romans shall fight as their allies with all their soul, as the occasion may prescribe for them.
verses.8:28: And to those who fight as allies there shall not be given grain, weapons, or silver, as it has seemed good to Rome; and they shall keep these obligations, and without deceit.
verses.8:29: According to these terms, thus have the Romans established it with the people of the Jews.
verses.8:30: Yet if after these terms both the one party and the other should decide to add or to take away anything, they shall do so of their own choice, and whatever they may add or take away shall be binding.
verses.8:31: Moreover, concerning the evils which King Demetrius is committing against them, we have written to him, saying, 'Why have you made your yoke heavy upon our friends and allies, the Jews?
verses.8:32: Therefore, if they appeal against you again, we will execute justice for them, and we will wage war against you by sea and by land.'"
verses.9:1: And Demetrius heard that Nicanor and his forces had waged war, and he proceeded to send Bacchides and Alcimus a second time into the land of Judah, and the right wing with them.
verses.9:2: And they went by the way to Gilgal, and encamped against Messaloth, which is in Arbela, and captured it, and he destroyed many lives of men.
verses.9:3: And in the first month of the one hundred and fifty-second year, they encamped at Jerusalem.
verses.9:4: And they departed and marched to Berea with twenty thousand men and two thousand horsemen.
verses.9:5: Now Judas had encamped at Alasa, and three thousand chosen men were with him.
verses.9:6: And they saw the multitude of the forces, that they were many, and they feared exceedingly; and many slipped away from the camp, so that none of them remained except eight hundred men.
verses.9:7: And Judas saw that his army had melted away, and the battle pressed hard upon him; and he was broken in heart, because he had no time to gather them together.
verses.9:8: And he grew faint, and said to those who remained, "Let us arise and go up against our adversaries, if perhaps we may be able to fight against them."
verses.9:9: And they tried to turn him back, saying, "We shall by no means be able; rather, let us save our own lives for the present; let us return with our brethren and fight against them, for we are few."
verses.9:10: And Judas said, "Far be it from me to do this thing, to flee from them! And our time has drawn near; let us die with valor for the sake of our brethren, and let us not leave any reproach upon our glory."
verses.9:11: And the army moved out from the camp, and they stood ready to meet them; and the cavalry was divided into two parts, and the slingers and the archers went before the army, along with the foremost fighters, all the mighty men.
verses.9:12: Now Bacchides was on the right wing, and the phalanx drew near from both sides, and they sounded with the trumpets; and those who were with Judas also blew the trumpets themselves.
verses.9:13: And the earth shook because of their armies, and the battle was joined from morning until evening.
verses.9:14: And Judas saw that Bacchides and the main strength of the army were on the right side, and all who were courageous in heart rallied to him.
verses.9:15: And the right wing was crushed by them, and he pursued after them as far as Mount Azotus.
verses.9:16: And those on the left wing saw that the right wing had been crushed, and they turned back close upon the heels of Judas and those who were with him from behind.
verses.9:17: And the battle grew fierce, and many fell wounded on the one side and on the other.
verses.9:18: And Judas fell, and the rest fled.
verses.9:19: And Jonathan and Simon took up Judas his brother, and buried him in the tomb of his fathers in Modein.
verses.9:20: And they wept for him there, and all Israel lamented for him with a great lamentation, and they mourned many days and said,
verses.9:21: "How has the mighty one fallen, who saved Israel!"
verses.9:22: Now the rest of the acts of Judas, and of the wars, and of the valiant deeds which he performed, and of his greatness, were not recorded; for they were exceedingly many.
verses.9:23: And it came to pass after the death of Judas that the lawless emerged in all the borders of Israel, and all the workers of iniquity sprang up.
verses.9:24: In those days there came an exceedingly great famine, and the land went over to their side.
verses.9:25: And Bacchides chose the ungodly men and appointed them masters of the land.
verses.9:26: And they sought out and searched diligently for the friends of Judas, and brought them to Bacchides; and he took vengeance on them, and they mocked them.
verses.9:27: And there was great tribulation in Israel, such as had not been since the day that no prophet appeared to them.
verses.9:28: And all the friends of Judas assembled together and said to Jonathan,
verses.9:29: "Since your brother Judas has died, there is no man like him to go forth against the enemies and Bacchides, and against those who are hostile to our nation.
verses.9:30: Now therefore we have chosen you this day to be in his place our ruler and leader, to fight our battle."
verses.9:31: And Jonathan accepted the leadership at that time, and rose up in place of Judas his brother.
verses.9:32: And Bacchides learned of it, and sought to slay him.
verses.9:33: And Jonathan and Simon his brother and all who were with him learned of it, and they fled into the wilderness of Tekoa, and encamped by the water of the cistern of Asphal.
verses.9:34: And Bacchides learned of it on the Sabbath day, and he and all his army came across the Jordan.
verses.9:35: And he sent his brother, the leader of the multitude, and appealed to the Nabataeans, his friends, to entrust to them their abundant baggage.
verses.9:36: And the sons of Jambrin came out from Medeba, and seized John and all that he had, and departed with them.
verses.9:37: Now after these things they reported to Jonathan and Simon his brother, saying, "The sons of Jambrin are celebrating a great wedding, and are bringing the bride from Nadabath, a daughter of one of the great nobles of Canaan, with a great escort."
verses.9:38: And they remembered John their brother, and went up and hid themselves under the cover of the mountain.
verses.9:39: And they lifted up their eyes and looked, and behold, there was a tumult and much baggage; and the bridegroom came out, along with his friends and his brothers, to meet them with timbrels and musical instruments and many weapons.
verses.9:40: And they rose up against them from the ambush and slew them; and many fell wounded, and the rest fled into the mountain, and they took all their goods.
verses.9:41: And the wedding was turned into mourning, and the sound of their musical instruments into lamentation.
verses.9:42: And they executed vengeance for the blood of their brother, and returned to the mountain of the Jordan.
verses.9:43: And Bacchides heard of it, and came on the Sabbath day as far as the banks of the Jordan with a great force.
verses.9:44: And Jonathan said to his brethren, "Let us arise now and fight for our lives; for today is not like yesterday and the day before.
verses.9:45: For behold, the battle is before us and behind us; and the water of the Jordan is on this side and on that side, with marsh and thicket, and there is no place to turn aside.
verses.9:46: Now therefore cry out to heaven, that you may be delivered from the hand of our enemies."
verses.9:47: And the battle was joined; and Jonathan stretched out his hand to strike Bacchides, but he turned aside backward away from him.
verses.9:48: Then Jonathan and those who were with him leaped into the Jordan and swam across to the other side, but they did not cross the Jordan against them.
verses.9:49: And about one thousand men on the side of Bacchides fell on that day.
verses.9:50: And they returned to Jerusalem, and built fortified cities in Judea: the stronghold that is in Jericho, and Emmaus, and Beth Horon, and Bethel, and Thamnatha Pharathon, and Tephon, with high walls and gates and bars.
verses.9:51: And they placed a garrison in them to harass Israel.
verses.9:52: And they fortified the city, and Beth-zur, and Gazara, and the citadel, and placed forces in them and stores of provisions.
verses.9:53: And they took the sons of the leaders of the land as hostages, and placed them in the citadel in Jerusalem under guard.
verses.9:54: And in the one hundred and fifty-third year, in the second month, Alcimus commanded to tear down the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary; and he tore down the works of the prophets, and began to tear it down.
verses.9:55: At that time Alcimus was stricken, and his works were hindered; and his mouth was stopped, and he was paralyzed, and he was no longer able to speak a word or give command concerning his house.
verses.9:56: And Alcimus died at that time with great torment.
verses.9:57: And Bacchides saw that Alcimus had died, and he returned to the king; and the land of Judah had rest for two years.
verses.9:58: Then all the lawless took counsel together, saying, "Behold, Jonathan and those with him dwell in quietness and confidence; now therefore we will bring Bacchides, and he will seize them all in one night."
verses.9:59: And they went and took counsel with him.
verses.9:60: And he set out to come with a great force, and he sent letters secretly to all his allies who were in Judea, that they should seize Jonathan and those with him; but he was not able, because their plot became known to them.
verses.9:61: And they seized about fifty men from among the men of the country who were leaders of the wickedness, and he slew them.
verses.9:62: Then Jonathan and Simon and those with him withdrew to Bethbasi, which is in the wilderness, and he rebuilt its ruined parts and fortified it.
verses.9:63: And Bacchides learned of it, and gathered together all his multitude, and sent orders to those from Judea.
verses.9:64: And he came and encamped against Bethbasi, and fought against it many days, and made siege engines.
verses.9:65: And Jonathan left Simon his brother in the city, and went out into the country, and went with a small number.
verses.9:66: And he struck Odomera and his brothers and the sons of Phasiron in their encampment, and he began to strike and to go up with the forces.
verses.9:67: And Simon and those with him came out from the city and burned the siege engines.
verses.9:68: And they fought against Bacchides, and he was crushed by them; and they pressed him exceedingly hard, because his counsel and his assault were in vain.
verses.9:69: And they were enraged with wrath against the lawless men who had counseled him to come into the country, and they slew many of them; and he resolved to depart to his own land.
verses.9:70: And Jonathan learned of this, and sent ambassadors to him to make peace with him and to restore the captives to them.
verses.9:71: And he accepted, and did according to his words, and swore to him that he would not seek harm against him all the days of his life.
verses.9:72: And he restored to him the captives whom he had previously taken captive from the land of Judah; and he turned back and departed to his own land, and did not come again into their borders.
verses.9:73: And the sword ceased from Israel; and Jonathan dwelt in Michmash, and Jonathan began to judge the people, and he destroyed the ungodly out of Israel.
verses.10:1: And in the one hundred and sixtieth year, Alexander the son of Antiochus, Epiphanes, went up and took possession of Ptolemais; and they received him, and he reigned there.
verses.10:2: And King Demetrius heard of it, and he gathered exceedingly great forces and went out to meet him in battle.
verses.10:3: And Demetrius sent letters to Jonathan with peaceful words, so as to magnify him.
verses.10:4: For he said, "Let us be first to make peace with them, before he makes peace with Alexander against us;
verses.10:5: for he will remember all the evils which we have committed against him, and against his brothers, and against his nation."
verses.10:6: And he gave him authority to gather forces and to prepare weapons, and to be his ally; and he ordered that the hostages who were in the citadel be delivered to him.
verses.10:7: And Jonathan came to Jerusalem and read the letters in the ears of all the people and of those from the citadel.
verses.10:8: And they feared with a great fear when they heard that the king had given them authority to gather forces.
verses.10:9: And those from the citadel delivered the hostages to Jonathan, and they restored them to their parents.
verses.10:10: And Jonathan dwelt in Jerusalem, and began to build and renew the city.
verses.10:11: And he spoke to those who did the work, to build the walls and Mount Zion all around with squared stones for fortification; and they did so.
verses.10:12: And the foreigners who were in the strongholds which Bacchides had built fled;
verses.10:13: and each one left his place and departed to his own land.
verses.10:14: Only in Beth Zur were some left of those who had forsaken the law and the ordinances, for it was a place of refuge for them.
verses.10:15: Now King Alexander heard of all the promises that Demetrius had sent to Jonathan; and they recounted to him the battles and the valiant deeds which he and his brothers had done, and the toils which they had endured.
verses.10:16: And he said, "Shall we find even one such man? Now therefore let us make him our friend and ally."
verses.10:17: So he wrote letters and sent them to him according to these words, saying:
verses.10:18: "King Alexander to his brother Jonathan, greetings.
verses.10:19: We have heard concerning you that you are a man valiant in strength and worthy to be our friend.
verses.10:20: And now today we have appointed you high priest of your nation, and to be called the king's Friend"—and they sent him a purple robe and a golden crown—"and to support our cause and maintain friendship with us."
verses.10:21: So Jonathan put on the holy robe in the seventh month of the one hundred and sixtieth year, at the Feast of Tabernacles; and he gathered forces and prepared many weapons.
verses.10:22: And Demetrius heard these words, and he was grieved, and said,
verses.10:23: "What is this that we have done, that Alexander has forestalled us in securing friendship with the Jews as a support?
verses.10:24: I also will write to them words of encouragement, and of exaltation, and of gifts, that they may be with me for help."
verses.10:25: And he sent to them according to these words: "King Demetrius to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
