verses.10:26: Since you have kept the treaties with us, and have continued in our friendship, and have not gone over to our enemies, we have heard of it and rejoiced.
verses.10:27: And now continue still to keep faith with us, and we will repay you with good things in return for what you do with us.
verses.10:28: And we will grant you many remissions, and we will give you gifts.
verses.10:29: And now I release you and exempt all the Jews from the tributes, and from the salt tax, and from the crown levies;
verses.10:30: and instead of the third part of the sown crop, and instead of the half of the fruit of the trees which falls to me to receive, I remit from this day onward the taking of it from the land of Judah, and from the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.
verses.10:31: And let Jerusalem be holy and exempt, together with its borders, the tithes and the tolls.
verses.10:32: I also relinquish the authority over the citadel that is in Jerusalem, and give it to the high priest, that he may station in it men whom he himself shall choose, to guard it.
verses.10:33: And every soul of the Jews who has been taken captive from the land of Judah into all my kingdom I set free without ransom; and let all remit the tributes, even on their livestock.
verses.10:34: And all the feasts, and the Sabbaths, and new moons, and appointed days, and three days before a feast and three days after a feast—let all of them be days of immunity and release for all the Jews who are in all my kingdom.
verses.10:35: And no one shall have authority to exact payment from or trouble any of them concerning any matter.
verses.10:36: And let there be enrolled from the Jews into the forces of the king up to thirty thousand men, and allowances shall be given to them, as is due to all the forces of the king.
verses.10:37: And some of them shall be stationed in the great strongholds of the king, and some of them shall be appointed over offices of the kingdom that are positions of trust; and let their overseers and their rulers be from among themselves, and let them walk in their own laws, even as the king has commanded in the land of Judah.
verses.10:38: And as for the three districts that have been added to Judea from the country of Samaria, let them be annexed to Judea so as to be reckoned under one rule, not to obey any other authority except that of the high priest.
verses.10:39: Ptolemais and the territory adjoining it I have given as a gift to the sanctuary that is in Jerusalem, for the necessary expenses of the sanctuary.
verses.10:40: And I myself give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the king's revenues, from the appropriate places.
verses.10:41: And all the surplus which they had not paid from the funds, as in the former years, from now on they shall give for the work of the house.
verses.10:42: And in addition to this, the five thousand shekels of silver which they used to take from the revenues of the sanctuary, as in the former years, from the annual account—these also are remitted, because they belong to the priests who minister.
verses.10:43: And whoever flees to the temple that is in Jerusalem and within all its borders, owing royal dues or any other matter, let them be released, together with all that belongs to them in my kingdom.
verses.10:44: And for the building and the renewing of the works of the sanctuary, the expense also shall be given from the king's revenue.
verses.10:45: And for the building of the walls of Jerusalem, and fortifying it all around, the expense also shall be given from the king's revenue, and for the building of the walls in Judea."
verses.10:46: Now when Jonathan and the people heard these words, they did not believe them nor accept them, because they remembered the great evil that he had done in Israel, and how he had greatly afflicted them.
verses.10:47: And they were well pleased with Alexander, because he had been the author of peaceful words to them; and they fought as his allies all those days.
verses.10:48: And King Alexander gathered great forces and encamped opposite Demetrius.
verses.10:49: And the two kings joined battle, and the army of Demetrius fled; and Alexander pursued him and prevailed over them.
verses.10:50: And he pressed the battle exceedingly until the sun went down, and Demetrius fell on that day.
verses.10:51: Then Alexander sent ambassadors to Ptolemy, king of Egypt, according to these words, saying:
verses.10:52: "Since I have returned to my kingdom, and have sat upon the throne of my fathers, and have taken hold of the dominion, and have crushed Demetrius and gained mastery over our country,
verses.10:53: and I joined battle with him, and he and his army were crushed by us, and we have sat upon the throne of his kingdom—
verses.10:54: and let us establish friendship with him—now therefore give me your daughter as a wife, and I will become your son-in-law, and I will give to you and to her gifts worthy of you."
verses.10:55: And King Ptolemy answered, saying, "Good is the day on which you returned to the land of your fathers and sat upon the throne of their kingdom.
verses.10:56: And now I will do for you what you have written; only come to meet me at Ptolemais, that we may see one another, and I will become your father-in-law, even as you have said."
verses.10:57: So Ptolemy went out from Egypt, he and his daughter Cleopatra, and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.
verses.10:58: And King Alexander met him, and he gave him his daughter Cleopatra in marriage, and celebrated her wedding in Ptolemais, as kings do, with great glory.
verses.10:59: Now King Alexander wrote to Jonathan to come to meet him.
verses.10:60: And he went with glory to Ptolemais and met the two kings; and he gave them and their Friends silver and gold and many gifts, and found favor in their sight.
verses.10:61: And pestilent men from Israel, lawless men, assembled against him to bring charges against him; yet the king paid no attention to them.
verses.10:62: And the king gave command to them, and stripped Jonathan of his garments and clothed him in purple; and they did so.
verses.10:63: And the king seated him beside himself, and said to his officers, "Go out with him into the midst of the city and proclaim that no one shall bring charges against this man concerning any matter, and let no one trouble him for any reason."
verses.10:64: And it came to pass, when his accusers saw his glory as he had proclaimed it, and him clothed in fine linen, they all fled.
verses.10:65: And the king honored him, and enrolled him among the Chief Friends, and appointed him general and governor.
verses.10:66: And Jonathan returned to Jerusalem with peace and gladness.
verses.10:67: Now in the one hundred and sixty-fifth year, Demetrius, the son of Demetrius, came from Crete into the land of his fathers.
verses.10:68: And King Alexander heard of it, and he was exceedingly grieved, and returned to Antioch.
verses.10:69: And Demetrius appointed Apollonius, who was over Coele-Syria; and he gathered a great force and encamped at Jamnia.
verses.10:70: And he sent to Jonathan the high priest, saying, "You alone lift yourself up against us, and I have become a laughingstock and a reproach because of you. Why then do you exercise authority against us in the mountains?
verses.10:71: Now therefore, if you trust in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let us test our strength with one another there; for with me is the strength of the cities.
verses.10:72: Inquire and learn who I am, and the rest who help us; and they say, 'There is no foothold for you before our face, for twice your fathers were put to flight in their own land.'
verses.10:73: And now you will not be able to withstand the cavalry and such a force in the plain, where there is neither stone nor pebble, nor any place to flee."
verses.10:74: Now when Jonathan heard the words of Apollonius, his mind was stirred; and he chose ten thousand men and went out from Jerusalem, and Simon his brother met him to assist him.
verses.10:75: And he encamped against Joppa; and those of the city shut him out, because a garrison of Apollonius was in Joppa, and they fought against it.
verses.10:76: And those of the city were afraid and opened to him, and Jonathan gained mastery over Joppa.
verses.10:77: And Apollonius heard of it, and he marshaled three thousand cavalry and a great force, and marched toward Azotus as though passing through; and at the same time he advanced into the plain, because he had a multitude of cavalry and trusted in it.
verses.10:78: And he pursued after him to Azotus, and the armies engaged after him in battle.
verses.10:79: Now Apollonius had left one thousand cavalry secretly behind them.
verses.10:80: And Jonathan knew that there was an ambush behind him. And they surrounded his army and shot their arrows at the people from morning until evening.
verses.10:81: But the people stood firm, even as Jonathan had commanded; and their horses grew weary.
verses.10:82: Then Simon drew out his force and engaged the phalanx, for the cavalry was exhausted; and they were crushed by him and fled.
verses.10:83: And the cavalry was scattered in the plain; and they fled to Azotus and entered Beth Dagon, the temple of their idol, to save themselves.
verses.10:84: And Jonathan burned Azotus and the cities around it, and took their spoils; and the temple of Dagon and its sanctuary he burned with fire.
verses.10:85: And those who fell by the sword, together with those who were burned, amounted to about eight thousand men.
verses.10:86: And Jonathan departed from there and encamped against Ashkelon; and those of the city came out to meet him with great glory.
verses.10:87: And Jonathan returned with those who were with him, having many spoils.
verses.10:88: And it came to pass, when King Alexander heard these words, that he honored Jonathan even more.
verses.10:89: And he sent him a golden buckle, as is the custom to give to the Kinsmen of the kings; and he gave him Ekron and all its borders as an inheritance.
verses.11:1: And the king of Egypt gathered great forces, like the sand along the shore of the sea, and many ships; and he sought to seize the kingdom of Alexander by deceit, and to add it to his own kingdom.
verses.11:2: And he went forth into Syria with words of peace, and the people of the cities opened their gates to him and went out to meet him; for it was the command of King Alexander to meet him, because he was his father-in-law.
verses.11:3: Now as he entered into the cities of Ptolemais, he stationed forces as a garrison in each city.
verses.11:4: And when he drew near to Azotus, they showed him the temple of Dagon burned with fire, and Azotus and its surrounding towns demolished, and the bodies cast about, and those who had been burned, whom he had burned in the war; for they had made heaps of them along his way.
verses.11:5: And they recounted to the king what Jonathan had done, in order to cast blame upon him; but the king kept silent.
verses.11:6: And Jonathan met the king at Joppa with splendor, and they greeted one another and lodged there.
verses.11:7: And Jonathan journeyed with the king as far as the river called Eleutherus, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.11:8: Now King Ptolemy took mastery over the cities of the coast as far as Seleucia by the sea, and devised wicked schemes concerning Alexander.
verses.11:9: And he sent ambassadors to King Demetrius, saying, "Come, let us make a covenant with one another, and I will give you my daughter whom Alexander has, and you shall reign over the kingdom of your father;
verses.11:10: for I regret that I gave my daughter to him, for he sought to slay me."
verses.11:11: And he cast blame upon him because he coveted his kingdom.
verses.11:12: And taking his daughter away from him, he gave her to Demetrius; and the countenance of Alexander was changed, and their enmity became manifest.
verses.11:13: Then Ptolemy entered Antioch and put on the diadem of Asia; thus he placed two diadems around his head, that of Asia and of Egypt.
verses.11:14: Now King Alexander was in Cilicia during those times, because the people of those regions were in revolt.
verses.11:15: And Alexander heard of it and came against him in war; and Ptolemy marched out and met him with a strong hand, and put him to flight.
verses.11:16: And Alexander fled into Arabia to be sheltered there; and King Ptolemy was exalted.
verses.11:17: And Zabdiel the Arab cut off the head of Alexander and sent it to Ptolemy.
verses.11:18: And King Ptolemy died on the third day, and those who were in his strongholds perished at the hands of those in the strongholds.
verses.11:19: And Demetrius became king in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.
verses.11:20: In those days Jonathan gathered the men of Judea to assault the citadel that was in Jerusalem, and they built many engines of war against it.
verses.11:21: And certain men who hated their own nation, lawless men, went to the king and reported to him that Jonathan was besieging the citadel.
verses.11:22: And when he heard it, he was angry; and as soon as he heard it, he immediately broke camp and came to Ptolemais, and wrote to Jonathan that he should not besiege it, and that he should meet him to confer with him at Ptolemais with all speed.
verses.11:23: Yet when Jonathan heard this, he gave orders to continue the siege; and he chose some of the elders of Israel and of the priests, and put himself in peril.
verses.11:24: And taking silver and gold and garments and many other gifts, he went to the king at Ptolemais, and found favor in his sight.
verses.11:25: And certain lawless men from among the nation brought accusations against him.
verses.11:26: Yet the king dealt with him just as those before him had dealt with him, and exalted him in the presence of all his friends.
verses.11:27: And he confirmed to him the high priesthood and whatever other honors he had formerly possessed, and appointed him to be foremost among his first friends.
verses.11:28: And Jonathan requested the king to make Judea exempt from tribute, together with the three districts and Samaria, and they promised him three hundred talents.
verses.11:29: And the king consented, and wrote letters to Jonathan concerning all these things, after this manner:
verses.11:30: "King Demetrius to his brother Jonathan, greetings, and to the Jewish nation.
verses.11:31: The copy of the letter which we wrote to our kinsman Lasthenes concerning you, we have written to you also, that you may see it:
verses.11:32: 'King Demetrius to his father Lasthenes, greetings.
verses.11:33: We have determined to do good to the nation of the Jews, our friends, who observe what is right toward us, because of their goodwill toward us.
verses.11:34: Therefore we have confirmed to them the borders of Judea and the three districts of Aphaerema, Lydda, and Rathamin—they have been added to Judea from Samaria—and all that belongs to them, for all who offer sacrifice in Jerusalem, instead of the royal dues which the king formerly received from them year by year from the produce of the earth and the fruit of the trees.
verses.11:35: And as for the other things belonging to us from this time forward—the tithes and the tolls belonging to us, and the salt lakes, and the crowns belonging to us—we will grant all of them to them.
verses.11:36: And not one of these things shall be annulled from this time forward for all time.
verses.11:37: Now therefore, take care to make a copy of these things, and let it be given to Jonathan, and let it be placed on the holy mountain in a fitting and conspicuous place.'"
verses.11:38: And King Demetrius saw that the land was quiet before him and that nothing opposed him; so he dismissed all his forces, each man to his own place, except the foreign troops whom he had recruited from the islands of the nations. Therefore all the forces from the days of the fathers became hostile toward them.
verses.11:39: Now Trypho was formerly one of those who had followed Alexander; and seeing that all the forces were murmuring against Demetrius, he went to Sinmalcue the Arab, who was bringing up Antiochus, the young child of Alexander.
verses.11:40: And he pressed him persistently that he might hand the child over to him, so that he might reign in place of his father; and they reported to him all that Demetrius had done and the hatred which his forces held against him; and he remained there many days.
verses.11:41: And Jonathan sent word to King Demetrius that he should remove those in the citadel from Jerusalem and those in the strongholds, for they were waging war against Israel.
verses.11:42: And Demetrius sent word to Jonathan, saying, "Not only will I do these things for you and your nation, but I will indeed honor you and your nation with great honor, if I obtain an opportunity.
verses.11:43: Now therefore, you will do well to send us men who will fight alongside me, because all my forces have revolted."
verses.11:44: So Jonathan sent three thousand men, mighty in their strength, to Antioch; and they came to the king, and the king rejoiced at their arrival.
verses.11:45: And the people of the city gathered together into the midst of the city, about one hundred and twenty thousand men, and they wanted to slay the king.
verses.11:46: And the king fled into the palace, while the people of the city seized the thoroughfares of the city and began to fight.
verses.11:47: Then the king called the Jews for help, and they all rallied to him together; and they spread out through the city and slew in the city on that day about one hundred thousand.
verses.11:48: And they set the city on fire, and took much spoil on that day, and saved the king.
verses.11:49: And when the people of the city saw that the Jews had gained mastery over the city as they pleased, their courage failed, and they cried out to the king with supplication, saying,
verses.11:50: "Grant us the right hand of peace, and let the Jews cease fighting against us and the city."
verses.11:51: So they threw down their weapons and made peace; and the Jews were glorified before the king and in the sight of all who were in his kingdom, and they returned to Jerusalem carrying much spoil.
verses.11:52: Thus King Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom, and the land was quiet before him.
verses.11:53: Yet he proved false to all that he had said, and became estranged from Jonathan, and did not repay the favors which he had rendered to him, but afflicted him greatly.
verses.11:54: Now after these things Trypho returned, and with him Antiochus, a very young child; and he became king and put on a diadem.
verses.11:55: And all the forces whom Demetrius had dismissed in disgrace rallied to him; and they fought against him, and he fled and was routed.
verses.11:56: And Trypho captured the elephants and took possession of Antioch.
verses.11:57: Then young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan, saying, "I confirm to you the high priesthood, and appoint you over the four districts, and to be one of the friends of the king."
verses.11:58: And he sent him golden vessels and a table service, and gave him authority to drink from golden vessels, to wear purple, and to have a golden clasp.
verses.11:59: And he appointed his brother Simon commander from the Ladder of Tyre to the borders of Egypt.
verses.11:60: Then Jonathan went forth and marched through the region beyond the river and among the cities, and all the forces of Syria rallied to him as allies; and he came to Ashkelon, and the people of the city met him with great honor.
verses.11:61: And he went from there to Gaza, and the people of Gaza shut their gates against him; so he laid siege around it, and burned its surrounding towns with fire and plundered them.
verses.11:62: Then the people of Gaza appealed to Jonathan, and he granted them the right hand of peace; and he took the sons of their rulers as hostages and sent them to Jerusalem, and he passed through the country as far as Damascus.
verses.11:63: And Jonathan heard that the commanders of Demetrius had arrived at Kedesh in Galilee with a great force, intending to remove him from his office.
verses.11:64: So he went to meet them, but he left his brother Simon in the country.
verses.11:65: And Simon encamped against Beth-zur, and fought against it for many days, and shut it up.
verses.11:66: And they asked him to receive the right hand of peace, and he granted it to them; then he expelled them from there, took possession of the city, and set a garrison over it.
verses.11:67: Now Jonathan and his army encamped by the water of Gennesar, and they rose early in the morning and marched into the plain of Nasor.
verses.11:68: And behold, an army of foreigners met him in the plain, and they had set an ambush against him in the mountains while they themselves met him face to face.
verses.11:69: Then those in ambush rose up out of their places and joined battle; and all those who were with Jonathan fled.
verses.11:70: Not even one of them remained, except Mattathias the son of Absalom and Judas the son of Chalphi, commanders of the host of the forces.
verses.11:71: Then Jonathan tore his garments, put earth upon his head, and prayed.
verses.11:72: And he turned back against them in battle and routed them, and they fled.
verses.11:73: When those who had fled from him saw this, they returned to him and pursued with him as far as Kedesh, even to their camp, and encamped there.
verses.11:74: And about three thousand men of the foreigners fell on that day; and Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
verses.12:1: Now Jonathan saw that the time worked in his favor, and he chose men and sent them to Rome to confirm and renew the friendship with them.
verses.12:2: He also sent letters to the Spartans and to other places to the same effect.
verses.12:3: So they went to Rome and entered the senate house, and said, "Jonathan the high priest and the nation of the Jews have sent us to renew the friendship and the alliance for them, as before."
verses.12:4: And they gave them letters to those in each place, that they should escort them to the land of Judah in peace.
verses.12:5: And this is a copy of the letters which Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:
verses.12:6: "Jonathan, high priest of the nation, and the council of elders, and the priests, and the rest of the people of the Jews, to the Spartans their brethren, greetings.
verses.12:7: Even previously, letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Areius, who reigned among you, stating that you are our brethren, as the copy below sets forth.
verses.12:8: And Onias received with honor the man who was sent, and accepted the letters in which clear declaration was made concerning alliance and friendship.
verses.12:9: Therefore, though we have no need of these things, having as our comfort the holy books that are in our hands,
verses.12:10: we have endeavored to send to renew our brotherhood and friendship with you, that we might not become estranged from you; for many seasons have passed since you sent to us.
verses.12:11: We therefore, at every season without ceasing, on the feasts and on the other appointed days, remember you in the sacrifices which we offer and in our prayers, as it is right and fitting to be mindful of brethren.
verses.12:12: And we rejoice in your glory.
verses.12:13: As for us, many tribulations and many wars have surrounded us, and the kings around us have waged war against us.
verses.12:14: We did not wish, therefore, to trouble you or the rest of our allies and friends in these wars;
verses.12:15: for we have the help from heaven aiding us, and we were delivered from our enemies, and our enemies were humbled.
verses.12:16: Therefore we chose Numenius the son of Antiochus, and Antipater the son of Jason, and have sent them to the Romans to renew our former friendship and alliance with them.
verses.12:17: We commanded them therefore to go to you also and greet you, and to deliver to you our letters concerning the renewal and our brotherhood.
verses.12:18: And now you will do well to give us an answer regarding these matters."
verses.12:19: And this is the copy of the letters which they sent to Onias:
verses.12:20: "Ares, king of the Spartans, to Onias the great priest, greetings.
verses.12:21: It has been found in a writing concerning both the Spartans and the Jews that they are brethren, and that they are of the lineage of Abraham.
verses.12:22: And now, since we have come to know these things, you will do well to write to us concerning your peace.
verses.12:23: And we also write back to you: 'Your cattle and your possessions are ours, and what is ours is yours.' We therefore command that they report to you in accordance with these same words."
verses.12:24: Now Jonathan heard that the commanders of Demetrius had returned with a great force, larger than before, to wage war against him.
verses.12:25: So he departed from Jerusalem and met them in the country of Hamath, for he gave them no respite to set foot in his own land.
verses.12:26: And he sent spies into his camp; and they returned and reported to him that they were thus preparing to fall upon them during the night.
verses.12:27: Now when the sun went down, Jonathan commanded his men to keep watch and to remain under arms, being ready for battle throughout the whole night; and he stationed outposts all around the camp.
verses.12:28: And the adversaries heard that Jonathan and his men were prepared for battle; and they were afraid and trembled in their hearts, and they kindled fires in their camp.
verses.12:29: But Jonathan and his men did not know it until morning, for they saw the lights burning.
verses.12:30: Then he pursued after them, yet he did not overtake them, for they had crossed the river Eleutherus.
verses.12:31: So Jonathan turned aside against the Arabs who are called Zabadeans, and struck them down, and took their spoil.
verses.12:32: And breaking camp, he came to Damascus and marched through all the country.
verses.12:33: And Simon went out and marched as far as Ashkelon and the neighboring strongholds, and he turned aside to Joppa and occupied it beforehand.
verses.12:34: For he had heard that they intended to hand over the stronghold to the men of Demetrius; so he stationed a garrison there to guard it.
verses.12:35: Now Jonathan returned and assembled the elders of the people, and took counsel with them to build strongholds in Judea,
verses.12:36: and to raise the walls of Jerusalem higher, and to erect a great height between the citadel and the city to separate it from the city, so that it might stand alone, that they might neither buy nor sell.
verses.12:37: So they gathered together to build, and part of the wall of the brook on the east fell down, and he repaired that which is called Chaphenatha.
verses.12:38: And Simon built Adida in the Shephelah, and fortified it with gates and bars.
verses.12:39: Now Trypho sought to reign over Asia and to put on the diadem, and to lay hands upon Antiochus the king.
verses.12:40: And he feared lest Jonathan would not permit him, and lest he should make war against him; so he sought a way to seize him to put him to death. And departing, he came to Bethsa.
verses.12:41: And Jonathan went out to meet him with forty thousand men chosen for battle, and came to Bethsa.
verses.12:42: Now Trypho saw that he had come with a great force, and he was afraid to lay hands upon him.
verses.12:43: So he received him with honor and commended him to all his friends, and gave him gifts, and commanded his friends and his forces to obey him in the same way.
verses.12:44: And he said to Jonathan, "Why have you wearied all this people, when there is no war between us?
verses.12:45: Now therefore send them away to their homes, and choose for yourself a few men who shall remain with you, and come with me to Ptolemais; and I will hand it over to you, along with the rest of the strongholds and the numerous forces and all those in charge of affairs; then I will turn back and depart, for this is why I have come."
verses.12:46: And trusting him, he did as he said, and dismissed the forces, and they departed to the land of Judah.
verses.12:47: But he kept with himself three thousand men; about two thousand he left in Galilee, while one thousand went with him.
verses.12:48: Now as soon as Jonathan entered Ptolemais, the men of Ptolemais shut the gates and seized him, and all who had come with him they slew with the sword.
verses.12:49: And Trypho sent forces and cavalry into Galilee, into the Great Plain, to destroy all the men of Jonathan.
verses.12:50: And they learned that he had been seized and had perished, along with those who were with him; so they encouraged one another and marched in close formation, ready for battle.
verses.12:51: And their pursuers saw that it was for their very lives, and they turned back.
verses.12:52: So they all came in peace to the land of Judah, and mourned for Jonathan and those who were with him, and were exceedingly afraid; and Israel mourned with a great mourning.
verses.12:53: And all the nations around them sought to destroy them completely, for they said, "They have no ruler and helper; now therefore let us make war against them, and we shall blot out their remembrance from among men."
verses.13:1: Now Simon heard that Trypho had gathered a great army to come into the land of Judah to destroy it.
verses.13:2: And he saw that the people were trembling and terrified; so he went up to Jerusalem and assembled the people.
verses.13:3: And he encouraged them, and said to them, "You yourselves know all the things that I and my brothers and the house of my father have done for the laws and the sanctuary, and the wars and the distresses.
verses.13:4: For this cause all my brothers have perished for the sake of Israel, and I alone have been left.
verses.13:5: And now far be it from me to spare my own life in any time of affliction, for I am no better than my brothers.
verses.13:6: Rather, I will avenge my nation and the sanctuary and our wives and our children, because all the nations have gathered together to destroy us out of hatred."
verses.13:7: And the spirit of his people was rekindled upon hearing these words;
verses.13:8: and they answered with a loud voice, saying, "You are our leader in place of Judas and Jonathan your brother.
verses.13:9: Fight our battle, and all that you say to us we will do."
verses.13:10: So he gathered all the men of war, and made haste to finish the walls of Jerusalem, and fortified it all around.
verses.13:11: And he sent Jonathan the son of Absalom, and with him a considerable force, to Joppa; and he drove out those who were in it, and remained there in it.
verses.13:12: Then Trypho departed from Ptolemais with a great army to enter the land of Judah, and Jonathan was with him under guard.
verses.13:13: But Simon encamped in Adida, facing the plain.
verses.13:14: And Trypho learned that Simon had risen up in place of Jonathan his brother, and that he was about to engage him in battle; so he sent envoys to him, saying,
verses.13:15: "On account of the silver which Jonathan your brother owed to the royal treasury, because of the offices he held, we are holding him in custody.
verses.13:16: And now send one hundred talents of silver and two of his sons as hostages, so that when he is released he will not revolt against us, and we will release him."
verses.13:17: And Simon knew that they were speaking to him with deceit, yet he sent the silver and the boys, lest he should incur great hostility with the people,
verses.13:18: saying, "Because I did not send him the silver and the boys, he perished."
verses.13:19: So he sent the boys and the one hundred talents; but he broke his word, and did not release Jonathan.
verses.13:20: And after these things Trypho came to invade the city and destroy it, and he marched around by the road to Adora; and Simon and his army marched along opposite him to every place wherever he went.
verses.13:21: Now those from the citadel kept sending messengers, urging him to come to him through the wilderness and to send them provisions.
verses.13:22: So Trypho prepared all his cavalry to come; but in that night there was exceedingly heavy snow, and he did not come because of the snow; so he departed and came into Gilead.
verses.13:23: And when he drew near to Bascama, he slew Jonathan, and he was buried there.
verses.13:24: Then Trypho turned back and departed to his own land.
verses.13:25: And Simon sent and took the bones of Jonathan his brother, and buried him in Modein, the city of his fathers.
verses.13:26: And all Israel lamented him with great lamentation, and mourned for him many days.
verses.13:27: And Simon built a monument over the tomb of his father and his brothers, and raised it high to be seen, with polished stone both behind and before.
verses.13:28: And he set up seven pyramids, one opposite another, for his father and his mother and his four brothers.
verses.13:29: And for these he made elaborate devices, setting great pillars all around them; and upon the pillars he made suits of armor for an everlasting name, and beside the suits of armor, carved ships, so that they might be seen by all who sail the sea.
verses.13:30: This is the tomb which he made in Modein, which stands to this day.
verses.13:31: Now Trypho dealt treacherously with Antiochus the younger king, and slew him,
verses.13:32: and reigned in his place, and put on the diadem of Asia, and brought great calamity upon the land.
verses.13:33: And Simon built up the stronghold of Judea, and walled it around with high towers and great walls and towers and gates and bars, and stored provisions in the strongholds.
verses.13:34: And Simon chose men and sent them to King Demetrius to grant relief to the country, because all the deeds of Trypho were plunder.
verses.13:35: And King Demetrius sent word to him according to these words, and answered him, and wrote to him a letter as follows:
verses.13:36: "King Demetrius to Simon the high priest and friend of kings, and to the elders and nation of the Jews: Greetings.
verses.13:37: We have received the golden crown and the palm branch which you sent, and we are ready to make a great peace with you, and to write to the officials in charge of affairs to grant you remissions.
verses.13:38: And whatever we have confirmed to you stands firm, and let the strongholds which you have built belong to you.
verses.13:39: Furthermore, we remit to you any oversights and offenses up to this present day, and the crown which you owed; and if any other tax was collected in Jerusalem, let it no longer be collected.
verses.13:40: And if any among you are qualified to be enrolled among our attendants, let them be enrolled, and let there be peace between us."
verses.13:41: In the one hundred and seventieth year the yoke of the Gentiles was lifted from Israel.
verses.13:42: And the people of Israel began to write in their documents and contracts, "In the first year of Simon, the great high priest and commander and leader of the Jews."
verses.13:43: In those days he encamped against Gaza, and surrounded it with encampments; and he built a siege engine and brought it up to the city, and struck one tower and captured it.
verses.13:44: And those who were in the siege engine leaped out into the city, and there was a great commotion in the city.
verses.13:45: And those in the city went up with their wives and children upon the wall, having torn their garments, and cried out with a loud voice, pleading with Simon to grant them the right hand of peace.
verses.13:46: And they said, "Do not deal with us according to our wicked deeds, but according to your mercy."
verses.13:47: So Simon came to terms with them, and did not fight against them; yet he expelled them from the city, and cleansed the houses in which the idols were, and thus he entered into it singing hymns and offering blessing.
verses.13:48: And he cast out of it all uncleanness, and settled in it men who observe the law; and he fortified it still more, and built for himself a dwelling place in it.
verses.13:49: Now those from the citadel in Jerusalem were prevented from going out into the country to buy and to sell; and they hungered exceedingly, and a great number of them perished by famine.
verses.13:50: Then they cried out to Simon to receive the right hand of peace, and he granted it to them; and he expelled them from there, and cleansed the citadel from its defilements.
verses.13:51: And he entered into it on the twenty-third day of the second month, in the one hundred and seventy-first year, with praise and palm branches, and with lyres and with cymbals and with harps, and with hymns and with songs, because a great enemy had been crushed out of Israel.
verses.13:52: And he ordained that they should observe this day every year. And he fortified still more the mountain of the temple which was beside the citadel, and he dwelt there, he and those who were with him.
verses.13:53: And Simon saw that John his son was a grown man, and he appointed him commander of all the forces; and he dwelt in Gazara.
verses.14:1: Now in the one hundred and seventy-second year, King Demetrius gathered his forces and marched into Media to obtain help for himself, that he might make war against Trypho.
verses.14:2: And Arsaces, the king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrius had entered his borders, and he sent one of his commanders to capture him alive.
verses.14:3: And he went forth and struck down the army of Demetrius, and seized him and brought him to Arsaces, who placed him in prison.
verses.14:4: And the land had rest all the days of Simon; he sought what was good for his nation, and his authority and his glory pleased them all those days.
verses.14:5: And along with all his glory, he took Joppa for a harbor and made an entrance to the islands of the sea.
verses.14:6: He enlarged the borders for his nation and gained mastery over the country.
verses.14:7: He gathered many captives and held dominion over Gazara, Beth Zur, and the citadel; he removed the defilements from it, and there was none who opposed him.
verses.14:8: They tilled their land in peace, and the earth yielded its produce, and the trees of the plains their fruit.
verses.14:9: Elders sat in the broad streets, all speaking together of good things, and the young men put on splendor and garments of war.
verses.14:10: He supplied provisions for the cities and equipped them with instruments of fortification, until the name of his glory was renowned to the end of the earth.
verses.14:11: He established peace upon the land, and Israel rejoiced with great gladness.
verses.14:12: And each man sat beneath his vine and his fig tree, and there was none to terrify them.
verses.14:13: No one remained in the land to make war against them, and their kings were crushed in those days.
verses.14:14: He upheld all the humble of his people; he diligently sought the law, and removed every lawless and wicked man.
verses.14:15: He glorified the sanctuary and multiplied the vessels of the sanctuary.
verses.14:16: Now it was heard in Rome, and even as far as Sparta, that Jonathan had died, and they were deeply grieved.
verses.14:17: But when they heard that Simon his brother had become high priest in his place, and that he held dominion over the country and the cities in it,
verses.14:18: they wrote to him on bronze tablets to renew with him friendship and the alliance which they had established with Judas and Jonathan his brothers.
verses.14:19: And these were read before the assembly in Jerusalem.
verses.14:20: And this is the copy of the letters which the Spartans sent: "The rulers and the city of the Spartans, to Simon the great priest, and to the elders, and to the priests, and to the rest of the people of the Jews, our brethren: greetings.
verses.14:21: The ambassadors who were sent to our people reported to us concerning your glory and honor, and we rejoiced at their coming.
verses.14:22: And we have recorded the things spoken by them in the decrees of the people as follows: 'Numenius the son of Antiochus and Antipater the son of Jason, ambassadors of the Jews, came to us to renew their friendship with us.
verses.14:23: And it pleased the people to receive the men with honor, and to place the copy of their words in the designated records of the people, that the people of the Spartans might have a memorial; and they wrote a copy of these things to Simon the high priest.'"
verses.14:24: After these things, Simon sent Numenius to Rome bearing a great golden shield of the weight of one thousand minas, to confirm the alliance with them.
verses.14:25: Now when the people heard these words, they said, "What thanks shall we render to Simon and his sons?
verses.14:26: For he and his brothers and the house of his father have stood firm, and have driven away in battle the enemies of Israel from them, and have established freedom for it."
verses.14:27: So they inscribed a record on bronze tablets and set them upon a pillar on Mount Zion. And this is the copy of the writing: "On the eighteenth day of Elul, in the one hundred and seventy-second year—that is, the third year under Simon the high priest,
verses.14:28: in Saramel, in a great assembly of the priests, the people, the rulers of the nation, and the elders of the country, it was made known to us:
verses.14:29: Whereas wars have often arisen in the country, Simon the son of Mattathias, a descendant of the sons of Joarib, and his brothers gave themselves to peril and withstood the adversaries of their nation, that their sanctuary and the law might be upheld, and with great glory they glorified their nation.
verses.14:30: Jonathan gathered their nation together and became their high priest, and then was gathered to his people.
verses.14:31: Then their enemies purposed to invade their country, to destroy their country and to stretch out their hands against their sanctuary.
verses.14:32: Then Simon arose and fought for his nation; he spent much of his own wealth, furnished arms to the men of the army of his nation, and paid them wages.
verses.14:33: He also fortified the cities of Judea, and Beth Zur on the borders of Judea, where the arms of the enemies had formerly been, and he stationed there a garrison of Jewish men.
verses.14:34: He also fortified Joppa by the sea, and Gazara on the borders of Azotus, where the enemies had formerly dwelt, and settled Jews there; and whatever was needed for their restoration he placed in them.
verses.14:35: And the people saw the faithfulness of Simon and the glory which he purposed to bring to his nation, and they appointed him their leader and high priest because he had done all these things, and for the righteousness and the faithfulness which he kept toward his nation, and because he sought in every way to exalt his people.
verses.14:36: In his days it prospered in his hands that the Gentiles should be removed from their country, as well as those in the city of David in Jerusalem, who had built themselves a citadel from which they went forth and defiled the surroundings of the sanctuary and inflicted a great wound upon its purity.
verses.14:37: He settled Jewish men in it and fortified it for the security of the country and the city, and he raised higher the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.14:38: King Demetrius also confirmed to him the high priesthood in accordance with these things,
verses.14:39: and made him one of his friends, and honored him with great glory;
verses.14:40: for it had been heard that the Jews are called friends and allies and brethren by the Romans, and that they had received the ambassadors of Simon with honor;
verses.14:41: and that the Jews and the priests were well pleased that Simon should be their leader and high priest forever, until a faithful prophet should arise;
verses.14:42: and that he should be commander over them, and that he should have charge of the sanctuary, and that by his authority men should be appointed over their works, and over the country, and over the arms, and over the strongholds;
verses.14:43: and that he should have charge of the sanctuary, and that he should be obeyed by all, and that all documents in the country should be written in his name, and that he should be clothed in purple and wear gold.
verses.14:44: And it shall not be lawful for any of the people or of the priests to annul any of these things, or to contradict what shall be spoken by him, or to convene an assembly in the country without him, or to be clothed in purple, or to wear a golden buckle.
verses.14:45: And whoever acts contrary to these things, or annuls any of them, shall be held guilty."
verses.14:46: And all the people consented to establish for Simon that he should act according to these words.
verses.14:47: And Simon accepted, and consented to serve as high priest, and to be commander and ethnarch of the Jews and the priests, and to preside over all.
verses.14:48: And they commanded that this writing be placed on bronze tablets, and that they be set up within the precinct of the sanctuary in a secure place;
verses.14:49: and that copies of them be placed in the treasury, that Simon and his sons might have them.
verses.15:1: And Antiochus, the son of King Demetrius, sent letters from the islands of the sea to Simon, priest and ethnarch of the Jews, and to all the nation.
verses.15:2: And their contents were after this manner: "King Antiochus to Simon, high priest and ethnarch, and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
verses.15:3: Whereas certain pestilent men have seized control of the kingdom of our fathers, I purpose to lay claim to the kingdom, that I may restore it as it was before; and I have enlisted a multitude of mercenary forces and fitted out ships of war.
verses.15:4: Moreover, I intend to disembark into the land, that I may execute vengeance upon those who have ruined our country and those who have laid waste many cities in the kingdom.
verses.15:5: Now therefore, I confirm to you all the remissions that the kings before me remitted to you, and whatever other remissions they remitted to you;
verses.15:6: to strike your own stamp as coinage for your country;
verses.15:7: and that Jerusalem and the sanctuary be free. And all the weapons that you have prepared, and the strongholds that you have built, of which you hold possession, shall remain yours.
verses.15:8: And every royal debt, and all royal dues that shall come hereafter, from this time forth and for all time, shall be remitted to you.
verses.15:9: And as soon as we have established our kingdom, we will honor you and your nation and the temple with great glory, so that your glory shall become manifest throughout all the earth."
verses.15:10: In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year, Antiochus went forth into the land of his fathers, and all the forces assembled to him, so that few were left with Trypho.
verses.15:11: And King Antiochus pursued him, and he came fleeing to Dor, which lies by the sea;
verses.15:12: for he knew that calamities had gathered together against him, and the forces had forsaken him.
verses.15:13: And Antiochus encamped against Dor, and with him were one hundred and twenty thousand men of war and eight thousand cavalry.
verses.15:14: And he surrounded the city, and the ships closed in from the sea; and he pressed the city hard from the land and from the sea, and did not permit anyone to go out or to come in.
verses.15:15: Now Numenius and those who were with him came from Rome, bearing letters to the kings and to the countries, in which these words were written:
verses.15:16: "Lucius, consul of the Romans, to King Ptolemy, greetings.
verses.15:17: The ambassadors of the Jews have come to us as our friends and allies, renewing the original friendship and alliance, having been sent by Simon the high priest and the people of the Jews;
verses.15:18: and they have brought a golden shield of five thousand minas.
verses.15:19: Therefore it has seemed good to us to write to the kings and to the countries, that they should not seek evil against them, nor make war against them and their cities and their lands, and that they should not ally themselves with those who make war against them.
verses.15:20: Moreover, we have resolved to accept the shield from them.
verses.15:21: If therefore any pestilent men have fled from their country to you, deliver them over to Simon the high priest, that he may punish them according to their law."
verses.15:22: And he wrote the same things to King Demetrius, and to Attalus, and to Arathes, and to Arsaces,
verses.15:23: and to all the countries, and to Sampsake, and to the Spartans, and to Delos, and to Myndus, and to Sicyon, and to Caris, and to Samos, and to Pamphylia and Lycia, and to Halicarnassus, and to Cos, and to Side, and to Aradus, and to Rhodes, and to Phaselis, and Gortyna, and Cnidus, and Cyprus, and Cyrene.
verses.15:24: And a copy of them he wrote to Simon the high priest.
verses.15:25: Now King Antiochus encamped against Dor a second time, continually bringing his forces against it and constructing siege engines, and he shut Trypho in from coming in and going out.
verses.15:26: And Simon sent to him two thousand chosen men to fight as his allies, together with silver and gold and abundant equipment.
verses.15:27: Yet he would not receive them, but annulled all that he had previously covenanted with him, and became estranged from him.
verses.15:28: And he sent to him Athenobius, one of his friends, to confer with him, saying, "You hold possession of Joppa and Gazara and the citadel in Jerusalem, cities of my kingdom.
verses.15:29: You have laid waste their borders, and inflicted great devastation upon the land, and taken dominion over many places in my kingdom.
verses.15:30: Now therefore, deliver up the cities that you have seized, and the tributes of the places over which you have taken dominion, in the borders outside Judea.
verses.15:31: Otherwise, give in place of them five hundred talents of silver, and for the destruction that you have wrought and the tributes of the cities, another five hundred talents; otherwise, they will come and make war against you."
verses.15:32: So Athenobius, the king's friend, came to Jerusalem, and saw the splendor of Simon, and a sideboard with vessels of gold and silver, and a great retinue; and he was astonished, and reported to them the words of the king.
verses.15:33: And Simon answered and said to him, "We have neither taken foreign land nor seized what belongs to others, but the inheritance of our fathers; at a certain time, however, it was unjustly held in possession by our enemies.
verses.15:34: But we, having the opportunity, lay firm hold upon our inheritance and that of our fathers.
verses.15:35: Now concerning Joppa and Gazara, you make demand: these inflicted a great blow upon the people and upon our land; for these we will give one hundred talents." And he did not answer him a word,
verses.15:36: but returned in anger to the king, and reported to him these words, and the splendor of Simon, and all that he had seen; and the king was filled with great wrath.
verses.15:37: Meanwhile, Trypho boarded a ship and fled to Orthosia.
verses.15:38: And the king appointed Cendebeus commander-in-chief of the coastal region, and gave him forces of infantry and cavalry.
verses.15:39: And he commanded him to encamp facing Judea; and he commanded him to build up Kedron and to fortify the cities, and to wage war against the people; while the king pursued Trypho.
verses.15:40: So Cendebeus came to Jamnia, and began to provoke the people, and to invade Judea, and to take the people captive and slay them.
verses.15:41: And he built up Kedron, and stationed horsemen and forces there, that they might go forth and raid the roads of Judea, just as the king had directed him.
verses.16:1: And John went up from Gazara and reported to Simon his father what Cendebeus was doing.
verses.16:2: Then Simon called his two eldest sons, Judas and John, and said to them, "I and my brothers and my father's house have fought the wars of Israel from youth until this day, and it has prospered in our hands to deliver Israel many times.
verses.16:3: But now I have grown old, while you, by mercy, are sufficient in years; take my place and that of my brother, and go forth and fight for our nation, and may the help from heaven be with you."
verses.16:4: And he chose out of the country twenty thousand men of war and horsemen, and they marched against Cendebeus and passed the night in Modein.
verses.16:5: And rising early in the morning, they marched into the plain; and behold, a great army came to meet them, both foot soldiers and horsemen, and a brook was between them.
verses.16:6: And he encamped opposite them, he and his people; and he saw that the people were afraid to cross over the brook, so he crossed over first; and the men saw him, and crossed over behind him.
verses.16:7: Then he divided the people, with the horsemen in the midst of the foot soldiers, for the cavalry of the adversaries was exceedingly numerous.
verses.16:8: And they sounded the trumpets, and Cendebeus and his camp were put to rout, and many of his men fell wounded; and those who remained fled into the stronghold.
verses.16:9: At that time Judas, the brother of John, was wounded; but John pursued them until he came to Kedron, which he had built.
verses.16:10: And they fled into the towers that were in the field of Azotus, and he burned it with fire; and there fell of them about one thousand men, and he returned to Judea in peace.
verses.16:11: Now Ptolemy, the son of Abubus, had been appointed commander over the plain of Jericho, and he possessed much silver and gold;
verses.16:12: for he was the son-in-law of the high priest.
verses.16:13: And his heart was lifted up, and he purposed to seize control of the country, and plotted deceitfully against Simon and against his sons, to do away with them.
verses.16:14: Now Simon was visiting the cities in the country and attending to their affairs, and he went down to Jericho—he and Mattathias and Judas, even his sons—in the one hundred and seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat.
verses.16:15: And the son of Abubus received them with deceit into the small stronghold called Dok, which he had built, and made a great banquet for them; and he concealed men there.
verses.16:16: And when Simon and his sons had become drunk, Ptolemy and those who were with him rose up, and took their weapons, and burst in upon Simon in the banquet hall, and slew him and his sons, and some of his servants.
verses.16:17: Thus he committed great ungodliness, and repaid evil for good.
verses.16:18: Then Ptolemy wrote these things and sent word to the king, that he should send forces to his aid, so that he might deliver up their country and the cities.
verses.16:19: And he sent others to Gazara to do away with John; and to the captains of thousands he sent letters to come to him, that he might give them silver and gold and gifts.
verses.16:20: And he sent others to seize Jerusalem and the mountain of the temple.
verses.16:21: But one ran ahead and reported to John at Gazara that his father and his brothers had perished, and said, "He has sent to slay you also."
verses.16:22: And when he heard it, he was greatly astounded; and he seized the men who had come to destroy him and slew them, for he knew that they were seeking to destroy him.
verses.16:23: Now the rest of the acts of John, and of his wars, and of the valiant exploits that he accomplished, and of the building of the walls that he built, and of his deeds,
verses.16:24: behold, these are written in the book of the chronicles of his high priesthood, from the time that he became high priest after his father.

notes.1:1: "Kittim" (Greek Chettiim), used in the Old Testament for Cyprus and the western Mediterranean coasts, here refers to Macedonia and Greece.
notes.1:10: The "one hundred and thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks" follows the Seleucid era (beginning in 312 BC), placing the accession of Antiochus IV Epiphanes in 175 BC.
notes.1:11: The Greek text shifts from a singular subject ("a lawless son") used collectively to plural verbs ("and they persuaded ... saying"). The Greek phrase "separated from them" literally uses a preposition (hypo) normally meaning "by."
notes.1:13: The Greek verb "they gave" is plural, referring to the king together with his royal court, whereas some later manuscripts read singular "he gave."
notes.1:29: "Two full years" reflects a Hebraism (literally "two years of days"). "Chief collector of tribute" translates a Greek rendering of a Hebrew title that may also reflect "commander of the Mysians" (compare 2 Maccabees 5:24).
notes.1:48: The Greek text reads the infinitive "and to profane" (bebelosai), sharing "their souls" as its object, whereas some manuscripts read the adjective "and profane" (bebelo) modifying "every unclean thing."
notes.1:54: The Greek text reads "the forty-fifth year," an abbreviated reference to (or omission of "one hundred" from) the one hundred and forty-fifth year of the Seleucid era (167 BC). "Abomination of desolation" echoes Daniel 9:27; 11:31; 12:11.
notes.1:59: The Greek distinguishes between the "pagan altar" (bomos) erected for idolatrous worship and the temple "altar" (thysiasterion) upon which it was built.
notes.1:62: The Greek text reads "were hanged" (ekremasthesan), continuing the account of verse 61, whereas many manuscripts read "stood firm" (ekrataiothesan).
notes.2:5: The Greek text reads Sapphous (Sapphus) as Jonathan's surname, whereas other manuscripts read Apphous (Apphus).
notes.2:8: The Greek text reads endoxos ("glorious" or "honored"), whereas other manuscripts and ancient versions read adoxos ("inglorious" or "dishonored") in keeping with the surrounding lament.
notes.2:22: The Greek text reads ton nomon ("the law") of the king, whereas other manuscripts read ton logon ("the words") of the king.
notes.2:23: The Greek text reads thymiasai ("to burn incense"), whereas other manuscripts read thysiasai ("to offer sacrifice").
notes.2:26: The Greek text gives the name of Zimri's father as Salom, corresponding to Salu in Numbers 25:14.
notes.2:51: The Greek text repeats doxan ("glory"), reading "great glory and everlasting glory," whereas other manuscripts read "great glory and an everlasting name."
notes.2:54: The Greek text reads hierosynes hagias ("a holy priesthood"), whereas other manuscripts read hierosynes aionias ("an everlasting priesthood").
notes.2:63: The Greek text omits "and tomorrow" before "he shall by no means be found," which appears in other manuscripts.
notes.2:66: The Greek text reads the second-person plural polemesete ("you shall fight") and plural laon ("of the peoples"), whereas other manuscripts read "he shall fight the battle of the people."
notes.3:15: The verb "proceeded" (Greek prosetheto) reflects a Septuagint Hebraism (from Hebrew yasaf, literally "added"), signifying either that Seron proceeded onward or that a host joined him.
notes.3:16: The Greek text here reads "Methoron" (Methoron), a textual variant for "Beth-horon" (Baithoron), which appears in verse 24.
notes.3:18: Throughout 1 Maccabees, "Heaven" (ho ouranos) serves as a reverent metonymy for God, who is then referred to as "He Himself" in verse 22.
notes.3:30: The idiom "as once and twice" means "as on former occasions," and the Greek sentence continues directly into verse 31.
notes.3:41: The Greek text here reads "servants" (paidas), whereas some other manuscripts read "fetters" (pedas) for binding captives.
notes.3:42: The Greek text reads "the words of the kingdom" (tes basileias), referring to the royal decrees, where other manuscripts read "of the king" (tou basileos).
notes.3:43: This Greek text preserves the shorter reading without the additional clause "and let us fight for our people" found in some manuscripts.
notes.3:48: A compressed Greek clause indicating that the Israelites consulted the book of the law for guidance in contrast to how the Gentiles sought direction from the images of their idols.
notes.4:12: The Greek text reads echomenous ("positioned close") rather than the variant erchomenous ("coming"), depicting Judas's forces already drawn up directly opposite the enemy camp.
notes.4:15: The Greek text reads "the plains of Judea" (Ioudaias), whereas some manuscripts read "Idumea" (Idoumaias).
notes.4:22: Greek allophyloi literally means "foreigners" and is the standard Septuagint designation for the Philistines, whose coastal plain lay adjacent to Azotus and Jamnia.
notes.4:23: The Greek text has a conjunction separating "purple" and "sea-purple" (kai porphyran kai thalassian), whereas some manuscripts omit the conjunction and read "sea-purple" as a single phrase.
notes.4:24: The Greek text reads literally "For His mercy is good forever" (Hoti kalon eis ton aiona to eleos autou), a shorter liturgical refrain than witnesses that include a second clause ("for He is good, for His mercy endures forever").
notes.4:33: The Greek text reads hoi idontes ("those who have seen") rather than the variant hoi eidotes ("those who know").
notes.4:38: The Greek text reads "our sanctuary" (to hagiasma hemon), preserving the first-person plural possessive pronoun omitted in some manuscripts.
notes.4:49: The Greek text reads "the altar of burnt offerings and of incense" (to thysiasterion ton holokautomaton kai thymiamaton), whereas some manuscripts omit "of burnt offerings and," referencing only the altar of incense.
notes.4:61: The Greek text reads literally "and they fortified it to guard Bethzur" (kai ochyrosan auto terein ten Bethsoura), where the pronoun "it" likely anticipates Bethzur as a fortified stronghold.
notes.5:3: The Greek text reads "in Judea" (ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ), whereas other witnesses read "in Idumea" (Ἰδουμαίᾳ), referring to the border region of Acrabattene.
notes.5:8: The Greek reads "Jaze" (Ἰάζην), a variant form of the Transjordanian city Jazer (Ἰαζήρ); "daughter towns" (θυγατέρας) reflects a Semitic idiom for surrounding dependent villages.
notes.5:13: Literally "in the places of Tubias" (ἐν τοῖς Τουβίου), referring to the region of Tob in Transjordan.
notes.5:15: The Greek shifts from third person ("against them," ἐπ᾽ αὐτούς) to first person ("to consume us," τοῦ ἐξαναλῶσαι ἡμᾶς), blending indirect and direct speech.
notes.5:22: The Greek text reads "the cities of Ptolemais" (τῶν πόλεων Πτολεμαίδος), whereas other manuscripts read "the gates of Ptolemais" (τῶν πυλῶν Πτολεμαίδος).
notes.5:43: The Greek text reads "before him" (ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ), whereas other manuscripts read "behind him" or "after him" (ὄπισθεν αὐτοῦ).
notes.5:50: The Greek text reads "the men of the city" (οἱ ἄνδρες τῆς πόλεως), whereas other witnesses read "the men of the army" (τῆς δυνάμεως).
notes.5:56: The Greek text reads "Zechariah" (Ζαχαρίας) here, whereas other witnesses—and verses 18 and 60—read "Azariah" (Ἀζαρίας).
notes.5:66: The Greek text reads "Samaria" (Σαμαρίαν); many commentators emend this to "Marisa" (Mareshah) on geographical grounds and from Josephus.
notes.5:67: The Greek uses singular pronouns ("he," βουλομένου αὐτοῦ ... αὐτόν), whereas other witnesses read plural ("they"), referring to the priests who went out recklessly.
notes.6:1: The Greek text reads "in Elymais" (ἐν Ἐλύμαις), treating Elymais as a district in Persia containing the wealthy city; some manuscripts omit the preposition and read Elymais as the name of the city itself.
notes.6:2: "Golden shields" translates Greek καλύμματα χρυσᾶ (lit. "golden coverings"), likely referring to decorative shields or shield-covers.
notes.6:21: The Greek text reads ἐξ αὐτοῦ ("from it," referring to the blockade or citadel), whereas some manuscripts read ἐξ αὐτῶν ("some of them").
notes.6:26: "And they have fortified the sanctuary and Beth-zur" construes "the sanctuary" with "fortified" in agreement with 6:7; some punctuate the Greek to read "to capture it and the sanctuary, and they have fortified Beth-zur."
notes.6:28: "Those in charge of the cavalry" renders the Greek idiom τοὺς ἐπὶ τῶν ἡνιῶν (lit. "those over the reins"), referring to cavalry commanders or charioteers.
notes.6:37: The Greek text reads "thirty-two men" (δύο καὶ τριάκοντα), a notably high number for a single elephant tower that many scholars regard as an early textual corruption influenced by the thirty-two elephants in 6:30; "Indian driver" renders ὁ Ἰνδὸς αὐτοῦ (lit. "its Indian").
notes.6:43: The Greek text gives Eleazar's surname as Savaran (Σαυαράν), a variant of Avaran (Αὐαράν) in 2:5.
notes.6:49: The Greek text omits an explicit object after "made" (other manuscripts add "peace") and has singular ἐξῆλθεν ("went out"), rendered collectively in agreement with the following plural "them" (αὐτοῖς).
notes.6:53: The Greek text reads ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις ("in the sanctuary"), whereas some manuscripts read ἐν τοῖς ἀγγείοις ("in the storage vessels" or "storehouses").
notes.7:1: The Greek text reads "fifty-first year," omitting "and one hundredth" found in other manuscripts (referring to the one hundred and fifty-first year of the Seleucid era, 162-161 BC).
notes.7:7: The Greek text has the aorist indicative "he has punished" (ekolasato) rather than the imperative "let him punish" (kolasato) found in other manuscripts.
notes.7:25: The Greek text omits the negative particle, reading "that he was able to withstand them," whereas other manuscripts read "that he was not able to withstand them."
notes.7:31: The Greek text reads the place name Charpharsarama, whereas other manuscripts read Capharsalama.
notes.7:32: The Greek text reads "five thousand" (pentakischilioi), whereas other manuscripts read "five hundred" (pentakosioi).
notes.8:2: Greek Galatai ("Galatians") refers broadly to Celtic peoples, encompassing here the Gauls conquered by Rome in northern Italy and Europe as well as the Galatians of Asia Minor.
notes.8:8: The Greek text names India, Media, and Lydia—likely an early transmission error for Ionia, Mysia, and Lydia ceded to Eumenes II in the Peace of Apamea—and reads plural "their finest lands."
notes.8:10: The Greek critical text preserves the repeated clause "and plundered them" both before and after the capture of the land and destruction of the strongholds.
notes.8:17: Greek Hakchos ("Accos") corresponds to the Hebrew priestly family name Hakkoz (1 Chronicles 24:10; Ezra 2:61).
notes.8:28: Unlike verse 26, the Greek here reads "to those who fight as allies" (probably referring to the enemy's allies, or an early textual variation for "those who wage war") and omits "ships" from the list of prohibited supplies.
notes.9:1: The Greek text here reads "that Nicanor and his forces had waged war" (following Codex Sinaiticus), whereas other manuscripts read "had fallen in battle."
notes.9:10: The Greek text omits the conditional particle "if," reading directly "And our time has drawn near" rather than "And if our time has drawn near."
notes.9:19: The Greek text reads singular "his brother" after the compound subject "Jonathan and Simon," whereas other witnesses read plural "their brother."
notes.9:33: The Greek text reads "Asphal," whereas other manuscripts read "Asphar" (similarly in v. 5 the Greek reads "Alasa" for "Elasa").
notes.9:35: The implied subject shifts back from Bacchides (v. 34) to Jonathan, whose brother is identified as John in v. 36; in vv. 36–37, the Greek reads "Jambrin" where other witnesses read "Jambri."
notes.9:42: The Greek text reads "the mountain of the Jordan," whereas other manuscripts read "the marsh of the Jordan."
notes.9:50: In vv. 50–53 the Greek text uses plural verbs (referring to Bacchides and his forces) where other witnesses use singular verbs; "Thamnatha Pharathon" appears without a conjunction between the two names, and "Emmaus" renders the Greek variant form Emmaoum.
notes.9:65: "With a small number" renders the literal Greek "by number" (arithmo), a Hebraism indicating a small, easily counted force.
notes.9:69: The Greek text shifts from plural verbs ("they were enraged" and "they slew") to the singular "he resolved" (Bacchides), whereas other witnesses use singular verbs throughout.
notes.10:1: The one hundred and sixtieth year follows the Seleucid era (153/152 BC). Alexander Balas claimed to be the son of Antiochus IV Epiphanes and assumed the same royal title.
notes.10:20: The Greek embeds a third-person narrative clause ("and they sent him a purple robe and a golden crown," with a plural verb) directly within Alexander's letter. "Friend" denotes an official Seleucid court rank.
notes.10:36: "Allowances" translates Greek xenia (maintenance stipends or provisions), whereas some manuscripts read opsonia ("wages").
notes.10:42: The Greek text includes "as in the former years" within this clause (echoing verse 41) regarding the five thousand shekels previously drawn from the sanctuary's revenues.
notes.10:54: The Greek text reads "with him" (pros auton), whereas many manuscripts read "with one another" (pros allelous).
notes.10:64: The Greek text reads "fine linen" (sindona), whereas other manuscripts read "purple" (porphyran, matching verse 62).
notes.10:77: Azotus is the Hellenistic Greek name for the Old Testament Philistine city of Ashdod.
notes.10:84: The Greek text reads "the temple of Dagon and its sanctuary" (kai to hieron autes), whereas other manuscripts read "and those who had fled into it."
notes.11:3: The Greek text reads "into the cities of Ptolemais" (genitive Ptolemaidos); other manuscripts read the nominative Ptolemaios ("as Ptolemy entered the cities").
notes.11:12: The Greek text reads "the countenance of Alexander was changed"; other manuscripts read "he became estranged from Alexander."
notes.11:18: The repetition refers to Ptolemy's garrison soldiers stationed inside the fortified cities being slain by the local inhabitants of those strongholds.
notes.11:28: The Greek text includes "and Samaria" alongside "the three districts" and uses the plural "they promised"; other manuscripts read "the three districts of Samaria" (as in verse 34) with the singular "he promised."
notes.11:35: "Crowns" (Greek stephanous) refers to the royal crown tax, a customary gold tribute paid to Hellenistic rulers.
notes.11:39: Sinmalcue is the distinct Greek spelling in this text (Greek Sinmalchoue); other manuscripts read Imalkue.
notes.11:50: "Grant us the right hand of peace" renders the Greek idiom literally meaning "give us right hands," a standard Hellenistic expression for granting a pledge or terms of peace (also in verses 62 and 66).
notes.11:56: "The elephants" translates Greek ta theria (literally "the beasts"), the regular term in 1 Maccabees for war elephants.
notes.11:67: Nasor is the distinct Greek form in this text representing the biblical Hazor in Upper Galilee.
notes.12:7: The Greek source spells the Spartan king's name Areius here and Ares in 12:20, referring historically to King Areus I of Sparta.
notes.12:26: The Greek reads "his camp" (singular, referring to Demetrius's camp), whereas other manuscripts read "their camp."
notes.12:28: The Greek source stops at "kindled fires in their camp" as a nocturnal decoy; some other manuscripts add "and withdrew."
notes.12:40: The Greek source reads "Bethsa" here and in 12:41, corresponding to Beth-shan (Beth-shean) in other textual witnesses.
notes.12:45: The Greek source reads "the numerous forces" (pollas), whereas some manuscripts read "the remaining forces" (loipas).
notes.13:18: The Greek text reads the first-person verb "I did not send," reflecting a shift in perspective within Simon's thought; other Greek manuscripts read the third-person "he did not send."
notes.13:21: The Greek text reads the singular "to him," likely an early transcriptional variant for the plural "to them," referring to the garrison in the citadel.
notes.13:39: "The crown" here refers to the crown tax, a customary monetary tribute owed to the Seleucid king.
notes.13:43: The Greek text reads "Gaza," whereas verse 53 names "Gazara"; many interpreters regard "Gaza" here as a textual variant for Gazara.
notes.14:28: "Saramel" transliterates Greek Saramel, widely understood to reflect a Hebrew phrase meaning either "prince of the people of God" (a title for Simon) or "court of the people of God." The Greek verb translated "it was made known to us" is literally third-person singular active ("he made known"), used impersonally.
notes.14:41: The decree confers leadership and the high priesthood upon Simon provisionally "until a faithful prophet should arise," reflecting the view that authoritative prophecy was awaited to render a final decision (compare 1 Maccabees 4:46).
notes.14:43: The clause "and that he should have charge of the sanctuary" repeats the nearly identical clause from verse 42, preserved here in accordance with the Greek source text.
notes.14:48: The Greek text reads "in a secure place" (en topo pisto, literally "a trustworthy place"), whereas other manuscripts read "in a conspicuous place" (en topo episemo).
notes.15:6: The Greek text omits the introductory verb 'and I permit you' found in some manuscripts, continuing the royal grant directly from verse 5.
notes.15:18: The Greek text reads 'five thousand minas' (pentakischilion), whereas many other manuscripts read 'one thousand minas' (compare 14:24).
notes.15:22: 'Arathes' reflects the Greek text's shortened spelling for Ariarathes V, king of Cappadocia.
notes.15:23: 'Sampsake' and 'Caris' reflect the spellings in the Greek text, generally identified with Lampsacus (or Sampsames) and Caria, respectively.
notes.15:31: The Greek text reads the third-person plural 'they will come and make war' (ekpolemesousin) rather than the first-person plural found in some witnesses; similarly in 15:39 it reads 'the cities' (tas poleis) rather than 'the gates.'
notes.16:3: 'By mercy' and 'the help from heaven' are reverential circumlocutions referring to God's gracious favor and divine aid.
notes.16:10: The Greek feminine singular pronoun 'it' (auten) refers to Azotus rather than to the towers.
notes.16:14: The Greek text includes 'and' before 'his sons,' rendered epexegetically here ('even his sons') to identify Mattathias and Judas as the sons who accompanied Simon.
notes.16:17: The Greek text reads 'ungodliness' (atheian), whereas some manuscripts read 'treachery' (athesian).
